definition_zh: 被动的；消极的；被动语态的；无动力的
definition_en: accepting what happens without active response or resistance, relating to the grammatical passive voice, or describing something that works without power or motion of its own
core_image: 一个人坐在长椅上，任身旁的人来来去去，自己始终没有起身
scene: 午后的公交站，一个人坐在长椅上，看着一班班车过去却始终没有起身。He remained passive while the others argued about where to go.
sceneCN: 这里的 passive 是「消极的、不主动的」（第 1 个义项：不主动回应）；句意为别人争论要去哪里时，他始终不表态。图中可辨识物件：长椅、站牌、驶过的车。

pos.zh: 被动的；消极的；被动语态的；无动力的

derivatives.zh: 由 passive 加 -ly 构成，义为「被动地；消极地」
由 passive 加 -ity 构成，义为「被动；消极状态」
由否定前缀 im- 加 passive 构成，义为「无表情的；不动声色的」
由 passive 与 aggressive 复合而成，义为「消极对抗的」

senses.title: Accepting without active response
senses.definition: accepting what happens or what others do without acting, resisting or taking the initiative
senses.definitionCN: 对发生的事或别人的做法不作行动、不反抗、也不主动的
senses.example: He remained passive while the others argued about where to go.
senses.exampleCN: 别人争论要去哪里时，他始终不表态。
senses.why: Passive comes from the Latin word for suffering or undergoing, so the adjective first described someone who merely receives an action instead of starting one.
senses.whyCN: passive 来自拉丁语中表示「受苦、承受」的词，所以这个形容词最初形容只承受动作、不发起动作的人。

senses.title: Relating to the grammatical passive voice
senses.definition: describing a verb form or clause in which the subject receives the action rather than doing it
senses.definitionCN: 描述主语承受动作而不是发出动作的动词形式或从句
senses.example: The sentence was rewritten in the passive voice to sound more formal.
senses.exampleCN: 这个句子被改用被动语态，听起来更正式。
senses.why: Grammar borrowed the word because in a passive clause the subject is the one acted upon, exactly the role the adjective already named outside grammar.
senses.whyCN: 语法借用了这个词，因为在被动句里主语正是被作用的一方，这恰好就是形容词在语法之外早已指明的角色。

senses.title: Received from others rather than sought
senses.definition: describing something a person receives without acting, as in passive smoking or passive income
senses.definitionCN: 形容一个人并未主动争取而接受的东西，如被动吸烟或被动收入
senses.example: Children are most at risk from passive smoking at home.
senses.exampleCN: 儿童在家里受二手烟危害的风险最大。
senses.why: If the person is passive, whatever reaches them arrives without their effort, so smoking by others or money from investments is labelled passive from the receiver's side.
senses.whyCN: 如果人是被动的，那么来到他面前的一切都不是他努力得来的，于是别人吸烟或投资所得，都从接受者一方被叫作被动。

senses.title: Working without an outside power source
senses.titleCN: 无动力的；不消耗外部能源的
senses.definition: in technology, describing a device or system that works without an external power supply or moving parts
senses.definitionCN: 在技术领域，形容不靠外部电源或活动部件工作的装置或系统
senses.example: The building uses passive cooling instead of air conditioning.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋建筑采用被动式降温，而不使用空调。
senses.why: A passive component or a passive house simply sits there and lets physics do the work, so the old sense of receiving rather than acting fits machines as well as people.
senses.whyCN: 被动元件或被动式房屋只是待在那里，让物理规律去发挥作用，因此「承受而非施为」这个古老的意思，同样适用于机器。

intro.en: Passive comes from Latin passivus, capable of suffering or receiving an action, which was formed from the verb pati and reached English through Old French passif.
intro.cn: passive 来自拉丁语 passivus，意为「能受苦、能承受动作的」，由动词 pati 构成，经古法语 passif 进入英语。

items.en: Pati meant to suffer, to endure or to undergo, and it is the root behind passive, passion and patience.
items.cn: pati 意为受苦、忍受、承受，是 passive、passion 与 patience 共同的词根。

items.en: Passivus was a grammatical and philosophical term for what could receive an action rather than perform it.
items.cn: passivus 是语法与哲学用语，指能够承受动作而不是发出动作的东西。

items.en: Old French passif kept the sense of receiving and also named the passive voice in grammar.
items.cn: 古法语 passif 保留了「承受」之义，也用来指语法上的被动语态。

items.en: Middle English passive entered through grammar and philosophy, describing what is acted upon.
items.cn: 中古英语的 passive 经语法与哲学进入，形容被作用的一方。

items.en: Modern English extends the word to passive smoking, passive income and passive cooling, where no effort is made by the receiver.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个词扩展到被动吸烟、被动收入与被动式降温，接受者都不必出力。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the Latin root for suffering; the near-meaning group collects words for people who do not act, with one direct opposite.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「受苦」词根上的词；近义组收表示不行动者的词，并收入一个直接的反义词。

entries.definition: A very strong feeling; both words come from Latin pati, to suffer.
entries.definitionCN: 强烈的情感；两词同出拉丁语 pati（受苦）。

entries.definition: The ability to endure waiting without complaint.
entries.definitionCN: 毫无怨言地忍受等待的能力。

entries.definition: Showing no emotion or reaction on the face.
entries.definitionCN: 脸上不显露情绪或反应的。

entries.definition: Sympathy for another person's suffering.
entries.definitionCN: 对他人苦难的同情。

entries.definition: Not doing anything, or not working at the moment.
entries.definitionCN: 什么也不做，或暂时不运转的。

entries.definition: Willing to obey others without resistance.
entries.definitionCN: 愿意顺从他人而不反抗的。

entries.definition: Quiet and easy to control or teach.
entries.definitionCN: 安静、易于管束或教导的。

entries.definition: Doing things, taking initiative and making things happen.
entries.definitionCN: 做事、采取主动并推动事情发生的；passive 的反义词。

normalIntro.en: Passive is the grammar of receiving: its Latin root means to suffer or undergo, and the word keeps that shape whether it describes a person, a clause or a cooling system.
normalIntro.cn: passive 是「承受」的语法：它的拉丁词根意为受苦或承受，无论形容人、从句还是降温系统，这个词都保持这个形状。

normal.en: Passive and passion share the Latin root pati, to suffer: one is the state of being acted upon, the other is the feeling that comes with it.
normal.cn: passive 与 passion 共享拉丁词根 pati（受苦）：一个是承受动作的状态，一个是随之而来的情感。

normal.en: The passive voice puts the receiver first, which is why the object of an active sentence becomes the subject.
normal.cn: 被动语态把接受者放在前面，所以主动句的宾语变成了主语。

normal.en: Passive smoking is named from the non-smoker's side: the smoke arrives without being sought.
normal.cn: 被动吸烟是从不吸烟者一方命名的：烟是自己飘过来的，并非他去寻来的。

normal.en: Impassive is not passive plus a negative idea of weakness; it means the face shows nothing at all.
normal.cn: impassive 并不是「被动加懦弱」，它指脸上什么都不显露。

normal.en: Passive income still needs money or property behind it, so the word describes the receiver, not the absence of work.
normal.cn: 被动收入背后仍然需要资金或房产，所以这个词形容的是接受者，而不是没有付出。

abstract.en: A word whose root means to suffer reminds us that being acted upon is never entirely neutral.
abstract.cn: 一个词根意为「受苦」的词提醒人：被作用于身从来都不是完全中性的。

abstract.en: Grammar keeps a whole category for the receiver, which suggests that English finds it useful to say who was done to.
abstract.cn: 语法为接受者保留了一整个类别，这说明英语觉得说清「谁被怎么了」很有用。

abstract.en: A passive house and a passive person share one idea: letting forces already present do the work, for better or worse.
abstract.cn: 被动式房屋与被动的人共有一个想法：让已经存在的力量去发挥作用，无论好坏。

examples.en: He remained passive while the others argued about where to go.
examples.cn: 别人争论要去哪里时，他始终不表态。

examples.en: The sentence was rewritten in the passive voice to sound more formal.
examples.cn: 这个句子被改用被动语态，听起来更正式。

examples.en: Children are most at risk from passive smoking at home.
examples.cn: 儿童在家里受二手烟危害的风险最大。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「派西夫」——派西夫坐在长椅上一动不动，任事情自己发生；记住 passive 是被动的、消极的。

root: 来自拉丁语 passivus（能承受动作的），由动词 pati（受苦、承受）构成，经古法语 passif 进入英语；与 passion、patience 同根。

sensesIntro.en: The core is receiving rather than acting; the senses divide into a person who does not resist, the grammatical voice of the receiver, what arrives without being sought, and machines that work without power.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是承受而非施为；义项按「不反抗的人」「语法上接受者的语态」「不请自来的东西」「不耗动力的装置」分出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person sitting on a bench while others come and go, never standing up.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人坐在长椅上，任身旁的人来来去去，自己始终没有起身。

branches.en: a bench where someone never stands up
branches.cn: 始终没人站起来的一条长椅

branches.en: folded hands during an argument
branches.cn: 争论中交叠着的一双手

branches.en: a sentence turned around to face its object
branches.cn: 被调转过来朝向宾语的一个句子

branches.en: smoke drifting toward a child at a table
branches.cn: 飘向桌边孩子的一缕烟

branches.en: a house cooled by shade and stone
branches.cn: 靠阴影与石头降温的一所房子

intro.en: The word is the Latin adjective of receiving, made from the verb for suffering and a suffix meaning having the quality of.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语中表示「承受」的形容词，由表示受苦的动词与表示「具有……性质」的后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin pati and passivus are recorded, and Old French passif follows them, so the Latin ancestry of passive is reliable.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pati 与 passivus 均有记录，古法语 passif 紧随其后，因此 passive 的拉丁世系是可靠的。

definition_zh: 护照；通行证；途径
definition_en: an official document that identifies you and lets you travel abroad; also a permit to pass through a place, or something that opens the way to an opportunity
core_image: 一本深色封面的小册子递进窗口，换来一次放行
scene: 机场的查验台前排着长队，旅客把证件从包里拿出来，等着印章落下。She handed her passport to the officer and waited for the stamp.
sceneCN: 这里是「护照」（第 1 个义项：出入国境时证明身份的官方证件）；句意是她把护照递给工作人员，等对方盖章放行。画面里可想到查验台、行李牌与印章。

derivatives.zh: 由 passport 与 control 复合而成，指边境对护照的查验环节
由 passport 与 photo 复合而成，指用于护照的证件照
由 passport 与表示「持有者」的 holder 复合而成，指护照持有人

senses.title: An official document for travelling abroad
senses.definition: an official document issued by a government that identifies you and allows you to travel to other countries
senses.definitionCN: 由政府签发、证明身份并允许你前往他国旅行的官方证件
senses.example: My passport expires next spring.
senses.exampleCN: 我的护照明年春天到期。
senses.why: The word joins passing and a port: the paper that once let a traveller through a harbour gate became the paper that lets a person cross a border.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把「通过」与「港口」拼在一起：最初让旅客通过港口关卡的文书，后来成了让人跨越国境的证件。

senses.title: A permit to pass through a place
senses.titleCN: 通行证；通过某地的许可
senses.definition: an official paper allowing a person or a ship to enter, leave or move through a particular place
senses.definitionCN: 准许某人或某船进出、通过某地的官方文书
senses.example: In the old harbour, no ship sailed without a passport from the governor.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧时的港口，没有总督签发的通行证，任何船都不能出海。
senses.why: Before modern borders existed, a passport was aimed at a gate or a harbour rather than at a country, and history books still use the word that way.
senses.whyCN: 在现代国界形成之前，passport 针对的是一道关口或一个港口，而不是整个国家，历史叙述里至今保留这层用法。

senses.title: A means of reaching something
senses.definition: something that makes it possible for you to go somewhere or to achieve something
senses.definitionCN: 使你得以进入某地或取得某种成就的东西
senses.example: A good command of English is a passport to better jobs.
senses.exampleCN: 良好的英语能力是获得更好工作的敲门砖。
senses.why: If a passport opens a border, then any paper, skill or contact that opens a door can borrow the name, because the movement from document to opportunity is the same.
senses.whyCN: 既然护照能打开国界，那么任何能打开一道门的证书、技能或人脉都可以借用这个称呼，因为「从证件到机会」的这一步是相同的。

intro.en: Passport fuses a verb of stepping with the Latin word for a harbour, and the paper it names has kept that gate-opening picture for six centuries.
intro.cn: passport 把表示「迈步」的动词与拉丁语里的「港口」合在一起，这个证件名称也因此把「打开关口」的画面保留了六百多年。

items.en: Passus was a step or a pace, naming the ground a foot could cover in one stride.
items.cn: passus 意为一步、一步的距离，指一只脚迈一次所跨过的地面。

items.en: The verb passare grew from that noun and meant to step, to go through or to go by.
items.cn: 动词 passare 由这个名词发展而来，意为迈步、穿过、从旁经过。

items.en: Old French passer carried the verb into everyday speech, and a compound of passer with port named a paper for passing a port.
items.cn: 古法语 passer 把这个动词带入日常语言，passer 与 port 组成的复合词则指准许通过港口的文书。

items.en: Medieval Italian passaporto recorded the same compound for a document that let a ship or a person leave a port, and French passed the form on to English.
items.cn: 中古意大利语 passaporto 记录了同样的复合词，指让船只或人员离开港口的文书，法语又把这一形式传给了英语。

items.en: Modern English keeps the travel document as the main sense and extends the word to anything that opens a way, from a skill to a good name.
items.cn: 现代英语以出入境证件为主要义项，并把词义扩展到任何能打开通路的东西，从一门技能到好名声。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the stepping verb or on the harbour noun; the near-meaning group collects papers that grant entry or permission.
note.cn: 形近组收的是建立在「迈步」动词或「港口」名词上的词；近义组收的是准许入境或授予许可的证件。

entries.definition: To go past a point, or to hand something to someone.
entries.definitionCN: 经过某一点；也指把东西递给别人。

entries.definition: A way through, or a section of a text or a journey.
entries.definitionCN: 通道；也指文章的一段或旅程的一段。

entries.definition: A person who happens to be walking past.
entries.definitionCN: 恰好从旁边走过的路人。

entries.definition: Out of date; no longer fashionable.
entries.definitionCN: 过时的；不再时髦的。

entries.definition: An official mark or sticker in a passport allowing entry to a country.
entries.definitionCN: 护照上准许进入某国的官方签注或贴纸。

entries.definition: An official document giving permission to do something.
entries.definitionCN: 准许做某事的官方文件。

entries.definition: A paper or file that records information and can prove identity.
entries.definitionCN: 记录信息、可用以证明身份的纸张或文件。

normalIntro.en: The word is a small machine of two parts: a verb for stepping and a noun for a harbour, locked together into one paper.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由两部分咬合成一台小机器：一个表示迈步的动词，一个表示港口的名词，合成同一张纸。

normal.en: Pass means to go by, and port means a harbour, so a passport is literally a paper for going through a port.
normal.cn: pass 意为经过，port 意为港口，所以 passport 字面上就是「通过港口的纸」。

normal.en: Airports still keep the old picture alive: passport control stands exactly where a gate would be.
normal.cn: 机场仍在延续这个旧画面：护照查验处就设在相当于关口的位置。

normal.en: The plural is regular, passports, because it is an ordinary countable noun.
normal.cn: 复数按规则加 s 写作 passports，因为它就是普通的可数名词。

normal.en: The phrase a passport to success shows how a document for borders turned into a word for opportunity.
normal.cn: a passport to success 这个说法显示出：一张管边界的证件如何变成了表示机会的词。

normal.en: The stress falls on the first syllable, so the two parts are spoken as one word rather than as pass and port.
normal.cn: 重音落在第一个音节，因此两个部分读起来是一个词，而不是分开的 pass 与 port。

abstract.en: A passport is a state promising, in ink and paper, that you may be let through.
abstract.cn: 护照是国家用油墨和纸张作出的承诺：你可以被放行。

abstract.en: Every border turns a small book into a key, which is why the same word can later mean any key.
abstract.cn: 每一道国界都会把一本小册子变成钥匙，所以这个词后来能指任何一把钥匙。

abstract.en: The word reminds us that permission is a thing you can hold in your hand and lose in a minute.
abstract.cn: 这个词提醒人：许可是可以握在手里、也能在一分钟内丢掉的东西。

examples.en: She showed her passport at the desk and was waved through.
examples.cn: 她在柜台出示护照，随即被示意通过。

examples.en: A second language can be a passport to work in another country.
examples.cn: 第二门语言可以成为到别国工作的途径。

examples.en: The old rule required every vessel to carry a passport from the port authority.
examples.cn: 旧时的规定要求每艘船都携带港务当局签发的通行证。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕死跑特」——出门在外最怕丢了它，还得赶紧跑；passport 就是护照。

root: 由古法语 passer（经过）与 port（港口）复合，源头可追到拉丁语 passus（一步）与 portus（港口）；本义是准许通过港口的文书。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a paper that opens a gate; the senses run from the travel document to the older harbour permit and then to any means of access.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一张能打开关口的纸；义项从出入境证件，到较早的港口通行许可，再到任何通往机会的途径。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small dark booklet handed through a window in exchange for a nod.
core.cn: 核心意象：一本深色封面的小册子递进窗口，换来一次点头放行。

branches.en: a queue at a border desk in the early morning
branches.cn: 清晨边检柜台前的一条长队

branches.en: a ship waiting for a stamped paper before it sails
branches.cn: 一条等着盖章文书才敢出海的船

branches.en: a language certificate placed on a job application
branches.cn: 一份语言证书放在求职材料上

branches.en: the same paper serving a traveller and a vessel
branches.cn: 同一张纸先后服务于旅客与船只

branches.en: a gate that opens first for a ship and later for a career
branches.cn: 先是向船只、后是向职业打开的一道门

intro.en: Two Latin pieces hold the word together: a noun for a step with its verb, and a noun for a harbour that English still uses on its own.
intro.cn: 两个拉丁成分撑起这个词：一个表示脚步的名词及其动词，一个表示港口的名词，后者英语至今单独使用。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: a paper allowing passage through a port

definition_zh: 过去；往昔；过去的；以前的；经过；超过
definition_en: the time before now; belonging to an earlier time; moving from one side of something to the other; later than or beyond a point
core_image: 身后一条已经走完的路，脚印还在，前面的路还没踩出来
scene: 老屋的墙上挂着一排褪色的照片，屋里的人坐在灯下翻看从前的日子。He rarely talks about his past, even with close friends.
sceneCN: 这里是「过去、往昔」（第 1 个义项：已经发生的时间）；句意是他很少谈起自己的过去，对亲近的朋友也一样。画面里有旧照片、台灯和翻动相册的手。

derivatives.zh: 由 past 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「已成为过去的状态」
由 past 与 due 复合而成，义为「逾期的；过期的」
由 past 与 master 复合而成，义为「老手；行家」

senses.title: The time before now
senses.definition: the time that has already happened, considered as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 已经发生过的全部时间，作为整体来看
senses.example: The village has changed a great deal in the past.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村子在过去发生了很大变化。
senses.why: Past began as the participle of the verb meaning to go by, and what has gone by is exactly what we call the past.
senses.whyCN: past 原本是表示「走过去」的动词的分词，凡是已经走过去的，正是一段时间意义上的「过去」。

senses.title: Gone by; belonging to an earlier time
senses.definition: describing something that existed or happened before now and is no longer as it was
senses.definitionCN: 描述在此刻之前存在或发生、如今已不再是原样的东西
senses.example: She met an old friend and they talked about past summers.
senses.exampleCN: 她遇到一位老朋友，两人聊起从前的夏天。
senses.why: Once the participle describes time that has gone by, it can stand before a noun and mark that thing as belonging to the gone-by time.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个分词用来描述「已经走过去的时间」，它就能放在名词前，把那件事物标成属于那段过去的时光。

senses.title: Beyond a point in space
senses.definition: moving from one side of a place or object to the other, and ending up beyond it
senses.definitionCN: 从某地或某物的一侧移到另一侧，最后落在它的那一边
senses.example: A bus went past the school without stopping.
senses.exampleCN: 一辆公交车经过学校却没有停。
senses.why: The idea of going by turns into a preposition of place: you move along the side and leave the point behind you.
senses.whyCN: 「从旁边走过去」这个意思后来变成表示位置的介词：你沿着旁边移动，把那个点留在身后。

senses.title: Later than a stated time or beyond a limit
senses.definition: later than a particular hour, or more than a particular amount or stage
senses.definitionCN: 晚于某个时刻，或多于某个数量、越过某个阶段
senses.example: It was past midnight when the last guest left.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一位客人离开时已经过了午夜。
senses.why: If you have walked past a mark on a road, you are now beyond it; applied to hours and numbers, the same picture gives the sense of exceeding a limit.
senses.whyCN: 如果你已经走过路上的某个标记，你就到了它之外；把这一画面用到钟点和数字上，就得到「超过某个界限」的意思。

intro.en: Past is the old participle of pass, so its history is the history of walking by, worn down into a word for time that has walked away.
intro.cn: past 是 pass 旧时的分词，它的历史就是「从旁边走过」的历史，最后磨成一个指「已经走掉的时间」的词。

items.en: Passus was a step or a pace, and it named the distance a foot could cover at one stride.
items.cn: passus 意为一步、一步的距离，指一只脚迈一次所跨过的长度。

items.en: The verb passare grew from that noun and meant to step, to go through or to go by.
items.cn: 动词 passare 由这个名词发展而来，意为迈步、穿过、从旁经过。

items.en: Old French passer carried the verb into everyday use, and its past participle passé meant gone by.
items.cn: 古法语 passer 把这个动词带入日常使用，它的过去分词 passé 意为「已经过去的」。

items.en: English took past from that participle, first as a form of the verb pass and then as an adjective and a noun.
items.cn: 英语从这一分词借入 past，先作动词 pass 的一种形式，随后作形容词和名词。

items.en: Modern English adds the prepositional uses, the grammatical term past tense, and the fixed phrase in the past.
items.cn: 现代英语又添出介词的用法、语法术语「过去时」，以及固定说法 in the past。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers relatives of the verb pass, including the French borrowing that gave English its participle; the near-meaning group gathers words for earlier time.
note.cn: 形近组收的是动词 pass 的同族词，包括把分词送给英语的那个法语借词；近义组收的是表示「较早时间」的词。

entries.definition: To go by, to move beyond, or to hand something over.
entries.definitionCN: 经过；越过；也指把东西递过去。

entries.definition: A way through, or a stretch of text or music.
entries.definitionCN: 通道；也指一段文字或音乐。

entries.definition: Someone who happens to walk past a place.
entries.definitionCN: 恰好从某处走过的路人。

entries.definition: No longer in fashion; dated.
entries.definitionCN: 过时的；不再时兴的。

entries.definition: Belonging to an earlier time or to a previous state.
entries.definitionCN: 属于较早时期或先前状态的；以前的。

entries.definition: Coming before the one mentioned or the present one.
entries.definitionCN: 在提到的那一个或现在这个之前的。

entries.definition: Belonging to a time that has gone, often used of days or years.
entries.definitionCN: 属于已逝时光的，常用于 days 或 years。

normalIntro.en: The word is a participle that learned to stand alone, so every sense still carries the small movement of walking by.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词本是一个学会独立站立的分词，所以每个义项里都还带着「从旁边走过去」的小动作。

normal.en: Past is the participle of pass: time that has passed is the past.
normal.cn: past 是 pass 的分词：已经过去的时间，就是 the past。

normal.en: Walk past a shop and you leave it behind, which is why the preposition means beyond.
normal.cn: 从一家店前走过，就把它留在身后，这就是这个介词表示「越过」的原因。

normal.en: Half past ten means the hour hand has walked past the ten mark.
normal.cn: half past ten 意为时针已经走过了十点那个刻度。

normal.en: The past tense is the verb form used for what has already happened.
normal.cn: 过去时是用来表示已经发生之事的动词形式。

normal.en: As a noun it takes a regular plural, pasts, when several different pasts are compared.
normal.cn: 作名词比较几种不同的过去时，复数按规则写作 pasts。

abstract.en: The past is not a place you can visit, only a direction you have already walked.
abstract.cn: 过去不是能去的地方，只是你已经走过的一个方向。

abstract.en: English uses one small word for time gone and space passed, hinting that memory and motion share a shape.
abstract.cn: 英语用同一个小词表示逝去的时间与走过的空间，暗示记忆与移动共享同一种形状。

abstract.en: To say something is past is to say the road behind you no longer pulls at your feet.
abstract.cn: 说某件事已经过去，等于说身后那条路不再拽着你的脚。

examples.en: The past is never as simple as it looks from here.
examples.cn: 过去从来不像从这里看上去那样简单。

examples.en: We drove past the old mill on the way home.
examples.cn: 回家的路上我们开车经过了那座老磨坊。

examples.en: It is half past nine, so the shop is already open.
examples.cn: 现在九点半，商店已经开门了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕斯特」——想起过去的事有点怕；past 就是过去。

root: 由古法语 passer 的过去分词 passé 演变而来，源头是拉丁语 passus（一步）与晚期拉丁语 passare（通过）。

sensesIntro.en: The core is movement that leaves a point behind; time that has left us becomes the noun, and space left behind becomes the preposition.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「把某个点留在身后」的移动；离开我们的时间成了名词，被留在身后的空间成了介词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a road already walked, footprints still visible behind the walker.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条已经走完的路，脚印还在走路人的身后。

branches.en: a lamp-lit room where old photographs are turned over
branches.cn: 灯下翻看旧照片的房间

branches.en: a summer remembered by two old friends
branches.cn: 两位老朋友回忆起的某个夏天

branches.en: a bus sliding by a school gate without stopping
branches.cn: 一辆公交车驶过校门没有停

branches.en: a clock whose hands have left midnight behind
branches.cn: 指针已经把午夜留在身后的钟

branches.en: the same word marking old days and a road just walked
branches.cn: 同一个词既标出旧日，也标出刚走过的路

intro.en: The word is built from a Latin step and its verb, filtered through a French participle that English shortened.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语中表示「一步」的名词及其动词构成，经法语分词过滤，再由英语缩短而成。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

gone by; the time before now
the verb form used with have
items.meaningCN: 与 have 连用的动词形式

definition_zh: 糊状物；酱；面团；粘贴；痛打
definition_en: a soft wet mixture such as crushed food or an adhesive; also to stick something onto a surface, or in informal use to beat someone badly
core_image: 碗里一团湿润的糊被抹刀挑起，稳稳贴到另一面上去
scene: 厨房的案板上摊着一层细腻的糊，厨师用刀背把它抹平，再盖上一张薄纸。She mixed the flour with water until it formed a thick paste.
sceneCN: 这里是「糊状物」（第 1 个义项：柔软湿润的混合物）；句意是她把面粉和水搅成浓稠的糊。画面里有案板、抹刀和一只盛水的碗。

derivatives.zh: 由 paste 加 -y 构成，形容面色像糊一样苍白
由 paste 加 -ry 构成，指用面团烤成的糕点
由 tooth 与 paste 复合而成，指牙膏
由 paste 与 up 复合而成，指拼贴成的版面

senses.title: A soft, wet mixture
senses.definition: a soft wet substance made by crushing or mixing materials together
senses.definitionCN: 把材料碾碎或混合后形成的柔软湿润的物质
senses.example: Add a spoonful of tomato paste to the sauce.
senses.exampleCN: 往酱汁里加一勺番茄酱。
senses.why: The word came in as the name of dough, and dough is the first picture of a soft mass, so any soft mass can take the name.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是「面团」的名字，而面团就是柔软一团的最初画面，于是任何柔软的糊状物都能沿用这个称呼。

senses.title: Dough for pastry
senses.definition: a mixture of flour, fat and liquid, rolled out and baked into pastry
senses.definitionCN: 面粉、油脂与液体混合后擀开、烤成糕点用的面团
senses.example: The cook rolled the paste thin before cutting out the shapes.
senses.exampleCN: 厨师把面团擀薄，再切出各种形状。
senses.why: In older cooking, paste meant the dough itself, and that sense still lives in the names of baked goods made from it.
senses.whyCN: 在较早的烹饪语境里，paste 指的就是面团本身，这层意思至今还留在用面团做成的糕点名称里。

senses.title: To stick something onto a surface
senses.definition: to fix paper or another material onto a surface with paste or glue; also to place copied text or an image in a document
senses.definitionCN: 用浆糊或胶水把纸张等材料固定在某个表面上；也指把复制的文字或图像放进文档里
senses.example: She pasted the photograph into the middle of the page.
senses.exampleCN: 她把照片粘到了页面的正中。
senses.why: Once the noun names the sticky mixture, the verb naturally names the act of using it, and the computer menu extended that act to text and images.
senses.whyCN: 名词既指有黏性的糊，动词自然就指使用这种糊的动作；电脑菜单又把这个动作延伸到文字和图像上。

senses.title: To beat someone badly
senses.definition: to hit someone hard and repeatedly, or to defeat them easily, in informal speech
senses.definitionCN: 在口语中指狠狠地连打某人，或轻易击败对手
senses.example: The champion pasted his opponent in the second round.
senses.exampleCN: 冠军在第二回合把对手打得毫无还手之力。
senses.why: This rough sense is a separate informal development: hitting something until it flattens is imagined as pressing it into a paste.
senses.whyCN: 这层粗鲁的意思来自另一条口语发展线：把对方打到像被压成糊一样，于是用 paste 来形容痛打。

intro.en: Paste reaches English from a Greek word for barley porridge, by way of Latin dough and a French noun for a sticky mixture.
intro.cn: paste 从希腊语表示大麦粥的词出发，经由拉丁语的「面团」和法语表示黏稠混合物的名词，才进入英语。

items.en: Greek paste meant a barley porridge, a soft mass of grain and liquid; the related adjective pastos meant sprinkled.
items.cn: 希腊语 pastē 指大麦粥，即谷物与液体混合成的软团；相关形容词 pastos 意为「撒过的」。

items.en: Latin pasta named dough or a small cake of dough, and it kept the picture of something kneaded and soft.
items.cn: 拉丁语 pasta 指面团或面团做的小饼，保留了「揉过的柔软之物」这一画面。

items.en: Old French paste carried both the dough sense and the sense of a sticky mixture used to make things adhere.
items.cn: 古法语 paste 既有面团的意思，也有用来黏合东西的糊状物之意。

items.en: Middle English paste covered dough, pastry and the glue made from flour and water.
items.cn: 中古英语的 paste 兼指面团、糕点，以及用面粉和水调成的浆糊。

items.en: Modern English adds the verb, the computing sense of inserting copied material, and the informal sense of beating someone.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了动词用法、把复制内容插入文档的计算机义，以及「痛打」的口语义。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the dough family and its compounds; the near-meaning group collects sticky substances and soft food masses.
note.cn: 形近组收的是「面团」这一词族及其复合词；近义组收的是黏性物质与柔软的食品团块。

entries.definition: Italian food made from dough in many shapes.
entries.definitionCN: 用面团做成各种形状的意大利面食。

entries.definition: Dough baked with fat, or a sweet cake made from it.
entries.definitionCN: 加油脂烤成的面团，或用它做的甜点。

entries.definition: A folded pastry filled with meat or vegetables.
entries.definitionCN: 包着肉或蔬菜的折叠酥饼。

entries.definition: A soft substance used with a brush to clean teeth.
entries.definitionCN: 配合牙刷清洁牙齿的软膏状物。

entries.definition: A sticky liquid used to join materials together.
entries.definitionCN: 用来把材料黏合起来的黏稠液体。

entries.definition: A thick mixture of flour and liquid, ready to be baked.
entries.definitionCN: 面粉与液体混合、待烤的稠团。

entries.definition: A substance that makes two surfaces stick together.
entries.definitionCN: 使两个表面黏合的物质。

normalIntro.en: The word started as a name for soft dough and then spread to any soft mass, to glue, and to the act of sticking.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从「柔软的面团」出发，随后扩展到任何柔软的团块、胶，以及把东西粘上去的动作。

normal.en: Paste and pastry share the dough stem, so a bakery and a glue pot are distant cousins.
normal.cn: paste 与 pastry 共用「面团」这个词干，因此面包房和浆糊罐是远亲。

normal.en: Toothpaste keeps the old sense: a soft mass that is squeezed out and spread.
normal.cn: toothpaste 保留了旧义：挤出来再抹开的柔软一团。

normal.en: Copy and paste borrows the kitchen action of pressing one thing onto another.
normal.cn: copy and paste 借用了厨房里把一样东西按到另一样上的动作。

normal.en: The verb is regular: pasted, pasted, pasting.
normal.cn: 动词变化规则：过去式与过去分词都是 pasted，现在分词是 pasting。

normal.en: The informal sense of beating someone works by picturing the loser flattened like paste.
normal.cn: 口语里「痛打」的意思，是把输家想象成像糊一样被压扁。

abstract.en: Paste is matter that has given up its shape and can take any shape pressed into it.
abstract.cn: paste 是放弃了自身形状、可以被按成任何形状的物质。

abstract.en: Glue and dough are the same word because both are soft things that hold other things together.
abstract.cn: 胶与面团是同一个词，因为两者都是把别的东西黏住的软物。

abstract.en: A paste sits between solid and liquid, which is why the word slides so easily between food and glue.
abstract.cn: 糊处在固体与液体之间，所以这个词能在食物与胶之间轻易滑动。

examples.en: Stir the flour and water into a smooth paste.
examples.cn: 把面粉和水搅成细腻的糊。

examples.en: He pasted the two sheets of paper together with flour glue.
examples.cn: 他用面糊把两张纸粘在一起。

examples.en: A pat of almond paste makes a simple cake look finished.
examples.cn: 一小块杏仁膏就能让普通的蛋糕看起来完整。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「佩斯特」——把纸佩（贴）到墙上去；paste 就是粘贴。

root: 经古法语 paste 来自晚期拉丁语 pasta（面团），更早可追到希腊语 pastē（大麦粥）；同族词多与面团、糊状物有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a soft mass that can be spread or pressed; the senses divide into food masses, the sticky mixture, the act of sticking, and a rough slang use.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是可以抹开或压扁的柔软一团；义项分出食品团块、黏稠的糊、粘贴的动作，以及一层粗俗的口语用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lump of wet paste lifted on a knife and smoothed onto a surface.
core.cn: 核心意象：抹刀挑起一团湿润的糊，把它在平面上抹平。

branches.en: a spoon of tomato paste stirred into a simmering sauce
branches.cn: 一勺番茄酱搅进微沸的酱汁

branches.en: a rolling pin pressing dough into a thin sheet
branches.cn: 擀面杖把面团压成薄片

branches.en: a photograph fixed into the centre of a page
branches.cn: 一张照片被粘到页面正中

branches.en: a boxer flattened in the second round
branches.cn: 第二回合被打得毫无还手之力的拳手

branches.en: the same soft mass used as food and as glue
branches.cn: 同一团软物既当食物也当胶

intro.en: A Greek word for porridge, a Latin word for dough and a French noun for a sticky mixture all feed into this one short English word.
intro.cn: 希腊语的粥、拉丁语的面团与法语表示黏稠混合物的名词，共同汇入这个简短的英语词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 轻拍；轻压使成形；轻拍声；一小块（黄油）
definition_en: to touch someone or something lightly with a flat hand; also the light touch itself, its soft sound, or a small flat piece of butter
core_image: 手掌落下去又抬起，只留下一声轻响和一点温度
scene: 孩子跑过来抱住大人的腿，大人弯下腰，用手掌在他背上轻轻拍了两下。The nurse patted the child's shoulder and told him to breathe slowly.
sceneCN: 这里是「轻拍」（第 1 个义项：用手掌轻轻触碰，多表示安慰）；句意是护士轻拍孩子的肩膀，让他慢慢呼吸。画面里有弯腰的大人和被抱住的孩子。

collocations.zh: 拍拍某人的背以示鼓励

derivatives.zh: 由 pat 与 down 复合而成，指用手掌拍打式的搜身检查
由动词 pat 加 -ing 构成，作名词时指轻拍这一动作

senses.title: To touch lightly with a flat hand
senses.definition: to touch a person or animal gently with the flat of your hand, often to show affection or comfort
senses.definitionCN: 用手掌轻轻触碰人或动物，常用来表达亲切或安慰
senses.example: She patted the dog's head and it wagged its tail.
senses.exampleCN: 她拍了拍狗的头，狗摇起了尾巴。
senses.why: The word probably copies the sound of a light blow, so the first sense is the friendly, sound-sized touch itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个词很可能在模仿轻拍的声音，所以最早的意思就是这种亲切的、只有一声轻响的触碰。

senses.title: To press or shape something with light blows
senses.definition: to press something flat or into a shape using quick, light movements of the hand
senses.definitionCN: 用手快速而轻的动作把某物压平或压成某个形状
senses.example: Pat the dough into a round ball before you leave it to rise.
senses.exampleCN: 把面团拍成一个圆球，再放着让它发酵。
senses.why: From a friendly touch the same light blow turns into a working motion: the hand does not strike hard, it taps a shape into place.
senses.whyCN: 从亲切的触碰出发，同样轻的一下变成了干活的动作：手并不用力打，只是一下下把形状拍出来。

senses.title: A light blow or its sound
senses.definition: a quick light touch with the hand, or the soft sound it makes
senses.definitionCN: 手掌快速而轻的一下触碰，或它发出的轻微声响
senses.example: He gave the seat a pat to show that I should sit down.
senses.exampleCN: 他拍了拍座位，示意我坐下。
senses.why: The verb becomes a noun by naming one instance of the action, and because the blow is soft, the sound belongs to the sense as well.
senses.whyCN: 动词转成名词，只需指这一个动作的一次；因为这一下很轻，声音也就一并算进了词义。

senses.title: A small flat piece of butter
senses.definition: a small, roughly flat piece of butter or a similar soft food
senses.definitionCN: 黄油或类似软质食物的一小块，大致呈扁平状
senses.example: Melt a pat of butter in the pan before adding the eggs.
senses.exampleCN: 先在锅里化开一小块黄油，再倒入鸡蛋。
senses.why: Butter used to be shaped by hand into small flat pieces, so the word for a light blow came to name the piece you could pat out.
senses.whyCN: 过去黄油常被手工拍成小小的扁块，于是这个表示「轻拍」的词也用来指拍出来的那一小块。

intro.en: Pat has no secure ancient root: the verb is generally thought to imitate the sound of a light blow, and English records it from the Middle Ages onward.
intro.cn: pat 没有可靠的古老词根：一般认为这个动词模仿轻拍的声音，英语自中古时期起就有记录。

items.en: No secure older source is recorded; the verb is generally thought to be imitative of the sound of a light blow.
items.cn: 没有更早的可靠来源记录；一般认为这个动词模仿轻拍所发出的声音。

items.en: Forms such as patten appear in Middle English with the sense of striking or touching lightly.
items.cn: 中古英语中已出现 patten 一类形式，意为轻轻击打或触碰。

items.en: The noun pat names both the light blow and the small sound that comes with it.
items.cn: 近代英语早期，名词 pat 既指这一下轻拍，也指随之而来的轻微声响。

items.en: The phrase a pat of butter is recorded for a small flat piece shaped by patting.
items.cn: 十八世纪出现 a pat of butter 的说法，指拍成的一小块扁平黄油。

items.en: Modern English keeps the word informal and friendly, used for encouragement as well as for shaping things by hand.
items.cn: 现代英语中这个词仍带口语与亲切色彩，既用于鼓励，也用于用手把东西拍出形状。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers short words that echo the same sound or spelling; the near-meaning group gathers verbs for touching and stroking.
note.cn: 形近组收的是声音或拼写相近的短词；近义组收的是表示触碰与抚摸的动词。

entries.definition: A soft cushion or a thick piece of material; only the spelling is close, the source is different.
entries.definitionCN: 软垫或厚材料块；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: To make a rapid series of light tapping sounds.
entries.definitionCN: 发出连续快速的轻拍声。

entries.definition: A small flat cake of minced food; only the spelling is close, the source is different.
entries.definitionCN: 碎肉等做成的小扁饼；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: To hit something lightly and quickly, often with a finger.
entries.definitionCN: 常用手指轻而快地敲一下。

entries.definition: To move a hand slowly and gently over something.
entries.definitionCN: 用手缓慢轻柔地抚过某物。

entries.definition: To put a hand or an object lightly against something.
entries.definitionCN: 把手或物体轻轻放在某物上。

normalIntro.en: The word lives on sound and touch at once: a soft smack of the palm that is also a small act of kindness.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词同时活在声音与触感里：手掌轻轻的一下，也是一点小小的善意。

normal.en: Say pat and you almost hear the sound; the word is built on that soft smack.
normal.cn: 念出 pat，几乎就能听见那一声轻响；这个词就建立在这一下轻拍的声音上。

normal.en: A pat on the back is praise, because the same hand that comforts also congratulates.
normal.cn: a pat on the back 表示称赞，因为安慰人的那只手也用来道贺。

normal.en: Pat dry means to remove water with light touches rather than rubbing.
normal.cn: pat dry 意为用轻按的方式去掉水分，而不是用力摩擦。

normal.en: A pat of butter is the shape produced by patting a soft lump flat.
normal.cn: a pat of butter 就是把软块拍平后得到的形状。

normal.en: The verb doubles its final consonant: patted and patting, so the short vowel stays short.
normal.cn: 这个动词要双写末尾辅音：patted 与 patting，好让短元音保持短促。

abstract.en: A pat lasts less than a second but can carry more comfort than a long speech.
abstract.cn: 轻拍不到一秒，却能比一段长话带来更多安慰。

abstract.en: The word shows how language turns a sound into a gesture and a gesture into a piece of butter.
abstract.cn: 这个词显示了语言如何把声音变成动作，又把动作变成一块黄油。

abstract.en: Anything you can pat is small enough to be handled with care.
abstract.cn: 凡是能用手轻拍的东西，都小到值得被小心对待。

examples.en: She patted the child's back until he stopped crying.
examples.cn: 她轻拍孩子的背，直到他不再哭。

examples.en: Pat the dough flat with the palm of your hand.
examples.cn: 用手掌把面团拍平。

examples.en: He answered with a pat of butter and a slice of bread.
examples.cn: 他回答时递上一小块黄油和一片面包。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拍它」——轻轻拍它一下；pat 就是轻拍。

root: 来源不确定；一般认为模仿轻拍声的拟声词，中古英语已有 patten 一类形式，没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a light flat-handed touch; the senses run from comforting a person, to shaping an object, to the blow itself and the small piece it produces.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是手掌平放的一下轻触；义项从安慰他人，到把东西拍出形状，再到这一下本身以及拍出来的小块。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a palm coming down and lifting again, leaving a soft sound and a little warmth.
core.cn: 核心意象：手掌落下去又抬起，留下一声轻响和一点温度。

branches.en: a hand resting for a second on a child's back
branches.cn: 一只手在孩子背上停留片刻

branches.en: a palm pressing dough into a round shape
branches.cn: 手掌把面团按成圆形

branches.en: the small sound of a hand on a wooden seat
branches.cn: 手掌落在木椅上的轻微声响

branches.en: a curl of butter dropped into a hot pan
branches.cn: 一小块黄油落进热锅

branches.en: comfort and its quiet sound arriving together
branches.cn: 安慰与它轻轻的声音同时到达

intro.en: The word has no ancient root to unpack, so its parts are the English endings it picks up and the phrases it forms.
intro.cn: 这个词没有可拆解的古老词根，因此它的构词成分是它接上的英语词尾和组成的短语。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word; the imitative origin has no Latin family behind it.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录；它的拟声来源背后并没有一个拉丁词族。

definition_zh: 补丁；小块土地；斑块；修补；软件补丁
definition_en: a small piece of material sewn over a hole, a small area of ground or a spot of different colour, the act of mending with such a piece, or a small software fix
core_image: 膝盖破口上缝着的一方深色布片
scene: 旧屋的窗纸破了一角，老人从针线盒里剪下一块深色布。She sewed a patch over the hole in his jacket.
sceneCN: 这里的 patch 是「补丁、补片」（第 1 个义项：缝在破口上的那块布）；句意是她在他外套的破洞上缝了一块补丁。图中可辨识物件：针线盒、深色布片、磨破的外套。

pos.zh: 补丁；小块土地；斑块；软件补丁

derivatives.zh: 由 patch 加 -y 构成，义为「斑驳的；时好时坏的」
由 patch 与 work 复合而成，义为「拼布；拼凑之物」
由 patchy 加 -ness 构成，义为「不均；零散」

senses.title: A piece of cloth sewn over a hole
senses.definition: a small piece of material fixed over a hole or a worn place in clothes or fabric
senses.definitionCN: 缝在衣服或织物破洞、磨损处上方的一小块材料
senses.example: He wore a leather patch on the elbow of his coat.
senses.exampleCN: 他外套的肘部缝着一块皮补丁。
senses.why: Patch first named a piece cut to size, so the noun starts from the shape of the hole: what matters is the piece that fits it, not the mending itself.
senses.whyCN: patch 最初指剪好尺寸的一块东西，所以名词的起点是破洞的形状：关键是那块刚好合上的布，而不是缝补这件事。

senses.title: A small piece of ground
senses.definition: a small area of ground, especially one used for growing vegetables or flowers
senses.definitionCN: 一小块地面，尤指用来种菜或种花的
senses.example: They kept a vegetable patch behind the kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在厨房后面留了一小块菜地。
senses.why: Since a patch is a piece marked off from a larger surface, ground can be divided the same way, and a garden plot becomes a patch of earth.
senses.whyCN: 既然 patch 是从更大表面上划出的一小块，土地也能这样划分，于是一畦菜地就成了「一块」地。

senses.title: A spot of different colour
senses.definition: a small area of a surface that differs in colour or texture from the rest of it
senses.definitionCN: 表面上与其余部分颜色或质地不同的一小块区域
senses.example: A pale patch spread across the damp wall.
senses.exampleCN: 潮湿的墙上洇开了一块浅色斑。
senses.why: The same idea of a local piece applies to colour: a patch is where one shade covers a small area instead of the whole surface.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「局部一块」的念头也适用于颜色：patch 就是某一种色调只盖住一小片、而不是整面墙的地方。

senses.title: To mend with a piece
senses.definition: to cover a hole or worn place with a piece of material
senses.definitionCN: 用一块材料把破洞或磨损处盖住
senses.example: He patched the torn sail with a strip of canvas before the wind rose.
senses.exampleCN: 起风之前，他用一条帆布把破了的船帆补上。
senses.why: The verb is simply the noun put to work: to patch is to do what a patch does, laying one piece over a gap.
senses.whyCN: 动词就是把名词拿来用：to patch 就是做一块补丁所做的事，把一片东西盖在缺口上。

senses.title: A small software fix
senses.definition: a small piece of software added to a program to correct a fault or close a security hole
senses.definitionCN: 加在程序上的一小段软件，用来纠正故障或堵住安全漏洞
senses.example: The company released a patch for the security flaw within a day.
senses.exampleCN: 公司在一天之内就发布了修补这个安全漏洞的补丁。
senses.why: A flaw in a program is imagined as a hole, and the fix is imagined as a piece laid over it, so the cloth word moves into computing intact.
senses.whyCN: 程序里的缺陷被想象成一个洞，修好的办法被想象成盖上去的一片东西，于是这个缝补的词原封不动地走进了计算机领域。

intro.en: Patch is first recorded in Middle English as pacche, and its origin is uncertain; a link with Old French pieche, the ancestor of piece, is often suggested but cannot be proved.
intro.cn: patch 最早以 pacche 的形式见于中古英语，来源不确定；人们常说它与古法语 pieche（piece 的前身）有关，但无法证实。

items.en: The word appears in the fourteenth century as pacche, naming a piece of cloth set over a hole; no earlier form is securely recorded.
items.cn: 这个词在十四世纪以 pacche 的形式出现，指盖在破洞上的一块布；更早的形式没有可靠记录。

items.en: One common view connects it with Old French pieche, a piece or fragment, which would make it a distant relative of piece.
items.cn: 一种常见的看法把它与古法语 pieche（一块、碎片）联系起来，若成立，它便是 piece 的远亲。

items.en: Other scholars point to Low German and Middle Dutch words for a clout or a rag, suggesting the word was borrowed from trade speech rather than from French.
items.cn: 另一些学者指向低地德语与中古荷兰语中表示「破布、补块」的词，认为它来自商贸用语，而非来自法语。

items.en: By the sixteenth century the word also named a plot of ground, and the verb patched appeared beside the noun.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，这个词也能指一块地，动词 patched 也已在名词旁边出现。

items.en: Modern English keeps the cloth, land and colour senses, adds the computing sense in the twentieth century, and forms patchy and patchwork.
items.cn: 现代英语保留布料、土地与颜色三个义项，二十世纪又添上计算机义，并造出 patchy 与 patchwork。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the English words built on patch and two borrowings that only share its sound; the near-meaning group gathers words for mending and for small areas.
note.cn: 形近组收由 patch 构成的英语词，以及两个只是读音相近的外来词；近义组收表示「修补」与「小块区域」的词。

entries.definition: Covered with patches, or good in places and bad in others.
entries.definitionCN: 满是补丁的，或时好时坏的。

entries.definition: Cloth made by sewing many pieces together, or anything put together from parts.
entries.definitionCN: 用许多布片缝成的东西，或由各部分拼成之物。

entries.definition: To send something off or deal with it quickly.
entries.definitionCN: 发送；迅速处理。

entries.definition: A group of things made or handled together.
entries.definitionCN: 一批一起制作或处理的东西。

entries.definition: To repair something torn or broken, usually by sewing.
entries.definitionCN: 修补破损之物，通常用针线。

entries.definition: To put something damaged back into working order.
entries.definitionCN: 把损坏之物恢复到可用状态。

entries.definition: A small measured piece of ground, especially for growing things.
entries.definitionCN: 量好的一小块地，尤指种植用。

entries.definition: A small round mark or area of a different colour.
entries.definitionCN: 颜色不同的小圆点或小块区域。

normalIntro.en: Patch has no classical root to lean on, so its hooks come from the shape of a piece laid over a gap and from the English words built on it.
normalIntro.cn: patch 没有可依托的古典词根，所以记忆钩子来自「一片东西盖在缺口上」的形状，以及由它构成的英语词。

normal.en: Patchy is patch plus -y: something covered with patches looks uneven, so the adjective came to mean good in some places and bad in others.
normal.cn: patchy 是 patch 加 -y：盖满补丁的东西看上去不均匀，于是这个形容词引申为「有些地方好、有些地方差」。

normal.en: Patchwork is patch plus work: a whole surface made by sewing many separate pieces into one.
normal.cn: patchwork 是 patch 加 work：把许多分开的布片缝成一整块表面。

normal.en: Patch up keeps the cloth image for human affairs: to patch things up is to cover the tear in a relationship, not to weave new cloth.
normal.cn: patch up 把缝布的画面用到了人事上：修补关系是盖住那道裂口，而不是重新织一块布。

normal.en: The plural is patches with -es, because English adds -es after the ch sound.
normal.cn: 复数是 patches，加 -es，因为英语在 ch 音之后要加 -es。

normal.en: A software patch borrows the same picture: a small piece laid over a hole until a new version can replace the whole garment.
normal.cn: 软件补丁借用的是同一幅画面：先用一小片盖住漏洞，等新版本再把整件衣服换掉。

abstract.en: A patch never pretends the tear did not happen; it makes the damage visible and still keeps the garment in use.
abstract.cn: 补丁从不假装破口没发生过；它让损伤看得见，却仍让这件衣服继续可穿。

abstract.en: Because a patch is local, it teaches a modest kind of repair: fix the small place, leave the rest alone, and accept that the result will show.
abstract.cn: 因为补丁是局部的，它教的是一种克制的修补：只处理那一小处，别处不动，也接受修补的痕迹会留下。

abstract.en: Calling a plot of land a patch says that ownership is also a matter of drawing a boundary around a small piece of the earth.
abstract.cn: 把一块地叫作 patch，等于说「拥有」也是在土地上圈出一小片边界。

examples.en: He wore a leather patch on the elbow of his coat.
examples.cn: 他外套的肘部缝着一块皮补丁。

examples.en: They kept a vegetable patch behind the kitchen.
examples.cn: 他们在厨房后面留了一小块菜地。

examples.en: The company released a patch for the security flaw within a day.
examples.cn: 公司在一天之内就发布了修补这个安全漏洞的补丁。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕扯」——衣服破了个口，怕再扯大，就先缝上一块布；记住 patch 是补丁，也指一小块地。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a piece cut to fit a gap; the senses divide into the cloth piece, the piece of ground, the colour spot, the act of mending and the software fix.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是剪好尺寸、正好盖住缺口的一片东西；义项按「布料补片」「一块地」「色斑」「缝补动作」「软件补丁」分出。

definition_zh: 小路；小径；路线；路径；途径；道路
definition_en: a narrow way made for walking, the route along which someone or something travels, a course of action in life, or the chain of folders that locates a file
core_image: 湿叶覆盖的一条窄土路，尽头是湖
scene: 雨后的林子里，落叶铺满一条窄窄的土路，尽头通向湖边。We followed the path down to the lake.
sceneCN: 这里的 path 是「小路、小径」（第 1 个义项：供人行走的窄道）；句意是我们沿着这条小路走到湖边。图中可辨识物件：落叶、窄土路、湖面。

pos.zh: 小路；小径；路线；路径；途径

derivatives.zh: 由 path 与 way 复合而成，义为「通道；路径」
由 path 加否定后缀 -less 构成，义为「无路的」
由 path 与 finder 复合而成，义为「探路者；开创者」

senses.title: A narrow track for walking
senses.definition: a narrow way made for walking, especially across fields or through woods
senses.definitionCN: 供人行走的窄道，尤指穿过田野或树林的
senses.example: We followed the path down to the lake.
senses.exampleCN: 我们沿着这条小路走到湖边。
senses.why: Path in Old English named ground worn by feet, so the first sense is physical: a line that people make simply by walking it.
senses.whyCN: 古英语的 path 指被脚踩出来的地面，所以第一个义项是实体的：一条人走着走着就形成的线。

senses.title: The route from one place to another
senses.definition: the line along which someone or something moves or travels from one point to another
senses.definitionCN: 人或物从一地移动到另一地所经过的线
senses.example: The storm changed the path of the flight.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴改变了航班的航线。
senses.why: Once a track is seen from above as a line, it can belong to anything that moves, whether feet, a plane or a beam of light.
senses.whyCN: 一条小径从高处看就是一条线，于是它可以属于任何会移动的东西：脚步、飞机或一束光。

senses.title: A course of action in life
senses.definition: a way of living or acting that leads towards a particular result
senses.definitionCN: 通向某种结果的生活方式或行动方向
senses.example: She chose a path that her parents had never taken.
senses.exampleCN: 她选了一条父母从未走过的路。
senses.why: A route leads to a destination, and a career also has a direction, so the walking word is borrowed whenever a choice has a destination in view.
senses.whyCN: 路线通向目的地，人生也有方向，所以只要一个选择看得见终点，这个走路的词就会被借去使用。

senses.title: A location in a computer system
senses.definition: the set of folders that shows where a file is stored, or the route data takes through a network
senses.definitionCN: 标明文件存放位置的文件夹序列，或数据在网络中经过的路线
senses.example: Copy the file path into the search box.
senses.exampleCN: 把文件路径复制到搜索框里。
senses.why: A file sits at the end of a chain of folders, and that chain is read as a route, so the old walking word serves computing without changing shape.
senses.whyCN: 一个文件位于一串文件夹的末端，而这一串被读成一条路线，于是这个古老的走路词原样服务于计算机。

intro.en: Path goes back to Old English pæþ and to a West Germanic word for a track, reconstructed as patha; its deeper origin is uncertain, and it has no reliable Latin relative.
intro.cn: path 上溯古英语 pæþ，再上溯到一个表示「小径」的西日耳曼语词，重构形式为 patha；更早的来源不确定，也没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

items.en: A word reconstructed as patha named a track or a worn way, and it is the common ancestor of English path and German Pfad.
items.cn: 一个重构为 patha 的词表示小径或踩出来的路，它是英语 path 与德语 Pfad 的共同祖先。

items.en: Old English wrote the word pæþ and used it for a narrow way on the ground, with the th written by a runic letter.
items.cn: 古英语把这个词写作 pæþ，用来指地面上的一条窄路，其中的 th 音用一枚卢恩字母书写。

items.en: Middle English path kept the physical track and began to be used for the course of a journey or of a life.
items.cn: 中古英语的 path 保留实体的路径，并开始用来指一段行程或一生的走向。

items.en: Writers of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries made path to success and path of duty ordinary phrases.
items.cn: 十六、十七世纪的作者让「通往成功之路」与「责任之路」成为寻常说法。

items.en: Modern English adds the computing sense, where a path lists the folders passed through to reach a file.
items.cn: 现代英语添上计算机义：path 列出到达某个文件所经过的各个文件夹。

note.en: The look-alike group shows the compounds built on path and two Greek-derived words that merely share its spelling; the near-meaning group gathers words for tracks and routes.
note.cn: 形近组展示由 path 构成的复合词，以及两个只是拼写相近的希腊语来源词；近义组收表示小径与路线的词。

entries.definition: A path, or a course that leads from one state to another.
entries.definitionCN: 小径，或由一个状态通向另一个状态的途径。

entries.definition: A narrow path made for people on foot.
entries.definitionCN: 专供步行者走的窄道。

entries.definition: A quality in art or speech that stirs pity or sadness.
entries.definitionCN: 艺术或言辞中唤起怜悯与悲伤的特质。

entries.definition: Arousing pity, or so poor as to be contemptible.
entries.definitionCN: 引起怜悯的，或差得令人轻视的。

entries.definition: A rough path or the marks left by something moving.
entries.definitionCN: 崎岖的小道，或移动之物留下的痕迹。

entries.definition: A path through wild country, often narrow and unpaved.
entries.definitionCN: 穿过荒野的小径，通常狭窄且未铺砌。

entries.definition: The way taken from a starting point to a destination.
entries.definitionCN: 从起点到终点所走的路。

entries.definition: A road, a direction, or a method of doing something.
entries.definitionCN: 道路、方向，或做某事的方法。

normalIntro.en: Path is a native English word of uncertain deeper origin, and its hooks follow a line on the ground as it becomes a route, a life choice and finally a folder chain.
normalIntro.cn: path 是英语本族词，更早的来源不确定；记忆钩子顺着地面上的一条线，看它变成路线、人生选择，最后变成一串文件夹。

normal.en: Old English pæþ is the same word in older spelling, and the th was once written with a runic letter rather than two letters.
normal.cn: 古英语 pæþ 就是同一个词的旧拼写，其中的 th 一度用卢恩字母而不是两个字母书写。

normal.en: German Pfad and English path descend from one West Germanic word, which is why they look and sound like cousins.
normal.cn: 德语 Pfad 与英语 path 同出一个西日耳曼语词，所以它们看起来、听起来都像表亲。

normal.en: Pathway and footpath add a second noun instead of changing path itself, so the base word stays visible inside them.
normal.cn: pathway 与 footpath 都是再加一个名词，而不是改变 path 本身，所以基础词在它们里面仍然看得见。

normal.en: Pathless uses -less to say that no track exists, which is the same ending as in hopeless and careless.
normal.cn: pathless 用 -less 表示没有路，和 hopeless、careless 用的是同一个词尾。

normal.en: In computing a path is still a route: folders are places, and the path gives the order in which to pass through them.
normal.cn: 在计算机里，path 仍然是路线：文件夹是一个个地点，路径给出依次穿过的顺序。

abstract.en: A path is made by repetition: one walker leaves nothing, but enough feet wear a line into the ground.
abstract.cn: 路是被重复走出来的：一个人走过不留痕迹，脚足够多就把一条线磨进地面。

abstract.en: The word means both the line and the direction, which is why a life can be said to have a path without any ground under it.
abstract.cn: 这个词既指那条线，也指方向，所以人生即使脚下没有土地，也能说有一条 path。

abstract.en: Pathos looks like path but comes from Greek suffering, a reminder that two similar shapes can carry unrelated histories.
abstract.cn: pathos 看起来像 path，却来自希腊语中「受苦」一词，提醒人两个相似的形状可能背负毫不相干的历史。

examples.en: We followed the path down to the lake.
examples.cn: 我们沿着这条小路走到湖边。

examples.en: The storm changed the path of the flight.
examples.cn: 风暴改变了航班的航线。

examples.en: Copy the file path into the search box.
examples.cn: 把文件路径复制到搜索框里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爬石」——山间小路全是石头，得一步步爬过去；记住 path 是小路，也是路径。

root: 古英语 pæþ（小路）与德语 Pfad 同出西日耳曼语重构形式 patha，更早来源不确定；没有可靠的拉丁同族词，希腊语 pathos（受苦）只是拼写相近，与此词无关。

sensesIntro.cn: 核心是被脚踩出来的一条线；义项按「窄窄的小径」「任何移动之物的路线」「人生的走向」「文件的文件夹链」分出。

core.cn: 核心意象：湿叶覆盖的一条窄土路，尽头是湖。

branches.cn: 湿叶盖住的土路

branches.cn: 为避开风暴而改画的航线

branches.cn: 父母都没做过的选择

branches.en: a folder chain ending at one file
branches.cn: 以单个文件结尾的文件夹链

definition_zh: 耐心；耐性；毅力；单人纸牌游戏
definition_en: the ability to accept delay or trouble without becoming angry, the steady persistence needed for a long task, or a card game played by one person
core_image: 孩子弯着腰，一遍遍重系那根鞋带
scene: 孩子坐在门槛上，一遍遍把散开的鞋带重新系好，母亲在门口看着。Learning to tie a knot takes patience.
sceneCN: 这里的 patience 是「耐心、耐性」（第 1 个义项：能平静地等待与重复）；句意是学会系结需要耐心。图中可辨识物件：门槛、散开的鞋带、孩子的双手。

pos.zh: 耐心；耐性；毅力；单人纸牌游戏

senses.title: The ability to wait calmly
senses.definition: the ability to accept delay, trouble or suffering without becoming angry or upset
senses.definitionCN: 能够接受延误、麻烦或痛苦而不发怒、不烦躁的能力
senses.example: Learning to tie a knot takes patience.
senses.exampleCN: 学会系结需要耐心。
senses.why: Patience comes from Latin pati, to suffer, so waiting well is a mild form of bearing something unpleasant rather than a blank absence of feeling.
senses.whyCN: patience 出自拉丁语 pati（忍受），所以好好等待是一种轻微地承受不快，而不是没有感觉的空白。

senses.title: Steady persistence in a long task
senses.definition: the quality of continuing with something difficult for a long time without losing interest
senses.definitionCN: 长时间坚持做困难的事而不失去兴趣的品质
senses.example: Her patience with the experiment finally paid off.
senses.exampleCN: 她对这项实验的坚持终于有了回报。
senses.why: Endurance is not only waiting but continuing, and the same Latin root covers both because each one keeps bearing a cost as time passes.
senses.whyCN: 忍耐不只是等，还包括继续做下去；同一个拉丁词根同时覆盖两者，因为二者都在时间里持续承担代价。

senses.title: A card game for one player
senses.definition: a card game played by one person, known in American English as solitaire
senses.definitionCN: 一个人玩的纸牌游戏，美式英语中称为 solitaire
senses.example: He laid out a game of patience on the kitchen table.
senses.exampleCN: 他在厨房桌上摆开了一局单人纸牌。
senses.why: The game is named for the patience it demands: the player sits alone and waits for the right card to turn up.
senses.whyCN: 这种游戏得名于它对耐心的要求：玩的人独自坐着，等待合适的那张牌翻出来。

intro.en: Patience comes from Latin patientia, the noun of enduring built on pati, to suffer; Old French passed it to English as pacience, where it named both calm endurance and, later, a solitary card game.
intro.cn: patience 来自拉丁语 patientia，这是由 pati（忍受）构成的表「忍耐」的名词；古法语把它写作 pacience 传入英语，先指平静的忍耐，后来也指一种单人纸牌游戏。

items.en: Pati was the verb for suffering, undergoing or putting up with something, and it is the root shared by patient and patience.
items.cn: pati 是表示受苦、经历、忍受的动词，是 patient 与 patience 共有的词根。

items.en: Patientia was the noun for endurance and forbearance, formed from the participle patiens plus the noun ending -entia.
items.cn: patientia 是表示忍耐与宽容的名词，由分词 patiens 加名词词尾 -entia 构成。

items.en: Old French kept the word as pacience, with the meaning of calm endurance under delay or pain.
items.cn: 古法语保留为 pacience，意为在延误或痛苦之下平静地忍耐。

items.en: Middle English patience covered calm waiting and the bearing of hardship; the card game was added to the word in the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 中古英语的 patience 兼指平静的等待与对苦难的承受；单人纸牌这一义项在十八世纪才加上去。

items.en: Modern English keeps the noun patience for the quality, while patient serves as the matching adjective and as a noun for a sick person.
items.cn: 现代英语用名词 patience 表示这种品质，而 patient 则作对应的形容词，也作名词指病人。

note.en: The look-alike group lays out the words built on the same Latin participle so the noun and the adjective are not confused; the near-meaning group gathers other names for endurance and calm.
note.cn: 形近组把建立在同一拉丁分词上的词并排摆开，免得把名词与形容词弄混；近义组收表示忍耐与平静的其他说法。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning able to wait calmly, and the noun for a sick person.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词意为「有耐心的」，名词则指病人。

entries.definition: In a way that shows calm endurance of delay.
entries.definitionCN: 以平静忍耐延误的方式。

entries.definition: Unable to wait calmly, or eager for something to happen.
entries.definitionCN: 无法平静等待的，或急切盼望的。

entries.definition: The power to keep going through pain or hardship.
entries.definitionCN: 在痛苦或艰难中坚持下去的力量。

entries.definition: The willingness to accept things one dislikes or disagrees with.
entries.definitionCN: 愿意接受自己不喜欢或不赞同之事的度量。

entries.definition: The act of continuing firmly despite difficulty.
entries.definitionCN: 遇到困难仍坚定继续的行为。

entries.definition: A state of quietness in which anger and worry are absent.
entries.definitionCN: 没有怒气与焦虑的平静状态。

normalIntro.en: Patience is the noun of endurance built on the Latin verb to suffer, and its hooks show how bearing pain becomes calm waiting, long persistence and even a game played alone.
normalIntro.cn: patience 是建立在拉丁语「忍受」动词之上的表忍耐的名词，记忆钩子展示「承受痛苦」如何变成平静等待、长久坚持，乃至一个人的纸牌游戏。

normal.en: Pati is the Latin verb to suffer, so patience names the state of someone who bears something rather than someone who feels nothing.
normal.cn: pati 是拉丁语中「忍受」的动词，所以 patience 指承受着某物之人的状态，而不是毫无感觉。

normal.en: Patient is the adjective built on the participle patiens, while patience is the noun built on patientia; the pair differs in part of speech, not in root.
normal.cn: patient 是由分词 patiens 来的形容词，patience 是由 patientia 来的名词；这一对词性不同，词根相同。

normal.en: Impatient adds im-, meaning not, so an impatient person refuses to keep bearing the wait.
normal.cn: impatient 加上表示「不」的 im-，所以不耐烦的人是不肯继续承受等待的人。

normal.en: Patiently is patient plus -ly, and it describes the manner in which a delay is borne.
normal.cn: patiently 是 patient 加 -ly，描述的是承受延误的方式。

normal.en: The card game patience is named for the waiting it asks of a lone player, not for any rule of the game.
normal.cn: 纸牌游戏 patience 得名于它要求独自等待，而不是因为某条游戏规则。

abstract.en: Patience treats time as something that can be borne rather than spent, which is why the same word can mean waiting and persistence.
abstract.cn: patience 把时间看成可以承受的东西，而不是被花掉的东西，所以同一个词既能指等待，也能指坚持。

abstract.en: Because patience is a capacity, it can be kept, lost or worn thin, as if it were a material with a limited thickness.
abstract.cn: 因为 patience 是一种容量，它可以被保持、失去或磨薄，仿佛是一种厚度有限的材料。

abstract.en: The Latin root means to suffer, so patience is not indifference: it is endurance with the feeling left intact.
abstract.cn: 拉丁词根意为忍受，所以 patience 不是漠不关心：它是感觉仍然完好的忍耐。

examples.en: Learning to tie a knot takes patience.
examples.cn: 学会系结需要耐心。

examples.en: Her patience with the experiment finally paid off.
examples.cn: 她对这项实验的坚持终于有了回报。

examples.en: He laid out a game of patience on the kitchen table.
examples.cn: 他在厨房桌上摆开了一局单人纸牌。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「陪婶」——陪婶婶在车站等车，等再久也不催；记住 patience 是耐心。

root: 拉丁语 pati（忍受）构成分词 patiens（忍受着的，patient 的来源），再加 -entia 构成 patientia（忍耐，patience 的来源），经古法语 pacience 进入英语。patience 只能是名词；patient 与它同源，但可作形容词「有耐心的」，也可作名词「病人」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is bearing a cost as time passes; the senses divide into calm waiting, persistence in long work, and the solitary card game named for waiting.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是随时间推移而承受代价；义项按「平静的等待」「长任务中的坚持」「因等待而得名的单人纸牌」分出。

core.cn: 核心意象：孩子弯着腰，一遍遍重系那根鞋带。

branches.cn: 迟迟不动的队伍

branches.en: a mother watching a child try again
branches.cn: 看着孩子再试一次的母亲

branches.cn: 反复回到同一份样本的研究者

branches.cn: 第十次才系好的结

branches.cn: 独自在桌上摊开的纸牌

intro.en: The word is a Latin noun of endurance, reshaped by French; English also builds the matching adjective, its adverb and its negative from the same participle.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语中表示忍耐的名词，经法语改写；英语又从同一分词造出对应的形容词、副词与否定形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin pati and patientia are both recorded, so patience has a documented Latin ancestry shared with patient, patiently and impatient.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pati 与 patientia 均有记录，因此 patience 与 patient、patiently、impatient 共享有据可查的拉丁世系。

definition_zh: 病人；患者；有耐心的；能忍耐的
definition_en: a person receiving medical treatment, or an adjective meaning able to wait or bear difficulty without becoming angry
core_image: 诊所走廊里，老人抱着病历本等叫号

derivatives.zh: 由 patient 加 -ly 构成，义为「耐心地」
