senses.title: A person receiving medical care
senses.definition: a person who is receiving medical treatment, especially in a hospital or clinic
senses.definitionCN: 正在接受医疗诊治的人，尤指在医院或诊所里的
senses.example: The patient waited quietly for his name to be called.
senses.exampleCN: 那位病人安静地等着叫到他的名字。
senses.why: The noun comes from the same Latin participle: a sick person is literally the one who is suffering, the one who bears the illness.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词出自同一个拉丁分词：生病的人字面上就是「正在受苦的那一个」，是承受着疾病的人。

senses.title: Able to wait without annoyance
senses.definition: able to wait for a long time or accept delay without becoming annoyed
senses.definitionCN: 能够长时间等待或接受延误而不烦躁的
senses.example: Please be patient with the new trainee.
senses.exampleCN: 请对新来的实习生耐心一些。
senses.why: The adjective names the bearing of delay, so the old sense of suffering narrows to the mild discomfort of having to wait.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词指的是对延误的承受，于是「受苦」的旧义收窄为「不得不等待」这种轻微的不适。

senses.title: Able to endure provocation calmly
senses.definition: able to bear pain, provocation or difficulty without losing calm
senses.definitionCN: 能够承受痛苦、挑衅或困难而不失镇定的
senses.example: She stayed patient under a stream of rude questions.
senses.exampleCN: 在一连串无礼的提问下，她仍然保持忍耐。
senses.why: The original Latin sense of enduring pain survives in this use, where what must be borne is not time but pressure coming from other people.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语原本「忍受痛苦」的意思在这个用法里存活下来，只是要承受的不再是时间，而是来自他人的压力。

intro.en: Patient is the present participle of Latin pati, to suffer, passed through Old French pacient; English uses the same shape for the adjective and for the sick person, while the noun patience split off from Latin patientia.
intro.cn: patient 是拉丁语 pati（忍受）的现在分词，经古法语 pacient 传入英语；英语用同一个形状既作形容词，也指病人，而名词 patience 则从拉丁语 patientia 另分出来。

items.en: Pati meant to suffer, undergo or put up with, and it is the root behind both patient and patience.
items.cn: pati 意为受苦、经历、忍受，是 patient 与 patience 共同的词根。

items.en: Patiens was the present participle, literally suffering or enduring, and it could already be used as an adjective for someone who bears things well.
items.cn: patiens 是现在分词，字面意为「忍受着的」，已经能作形容词，形容善于承受的人。

items.en: From the same participle Latin built patientia, the noun of endurance, which became the English noun patience rather than the adjective.
items.cn: 拉丁语由同一分词构成名词 patientia，表示忍耐，它后来成为英语名词 patience，而不是形容词。

items.en: Old French kept pacient as both adjective and noun, and the noun could already mean a sick person under care.
items.cn: 古法语保留 pacient，兼作形容词与名词，其中的名词已经能指接受照料的病人。

items.en: Modern English keeps patient as an adjective and as a noun for the sick, and keeps patience as the separate noun for the quality.
items.cn: 现代英语让 patient 作形容词并指病人，又让 patience 作为独立名词表示这种品质。

note.en: The look-alike group puts the same-root noun, adverb and negative beside patient so the parts of speech stay distinct; the near-meaning group gathers words for calm bearing and for the sick person.
note.cn: 形近组把同根的名词、副词与否定式摆在 patient 旁边，以便分清词性；近义组收表示平静承受的词，以及指病人的词。

entries.definition: The noun for the ability to wait or endure calmly.
entries.definitionCN: 表示平静等待或忍耐能力的名词。

entries.definition: In a manner that shows calm endurance.
entries.definitionCN: 以平静忍耐的方式。

entries.definition: Unable to bear delay or waiting calmly.
entries.definitionCN: 无法平静承受延误或等待的。

entries.definition: Quiet and not showing worry, anger or excitement.
entries.definitionCN: 平静的，不显焦虑、愤怒或激动的。

entries.definition: Willing to accept differences and things one dislikes.
entries.definitionCN: 愿意接受差异与自己不喜欢之事的。

entries.definition: Lasting for a long time, or able to bear hardship.
entries.definitionCN: 持久的，或能承受艰难的。

entries.definition: A person who is affected by an illness or a bad situation.
entries.definitionCN: 受疾病或困境影响的人。

normalIntro.en: Patient is one Latin participle doing two jobs in English, and its hooks keep the sick person and the calm bearer tied to the same root.
normalIntro.cn: patient 是同一个拉丁分词在英语里兼做两件事，记忆钩子让「病人」与「平静承受者」都系在同一个词根上。

normal.en: Pati, to suffer, is the root of both patient and patience, so the sick person and the calm waiter share one history.
normal.cn: pati（忍受）是 patient 与 patience 共同的词根，所以病人与平静等待的人共享同一段历史。

normal.en: As a noun, patient is the one who suffers an illness; as an adjective, it is the one who bears a wait. One shape, two jobs.
normal.cn: 作名词时，patient 是承受疾病的人；作形容词时，是承受等待的人。一个形状，两份工作。

normal.en: Patience is the noun from patientia, so the pair differs in part of speech and not in origin.
normal.cn: patience 是出自 patientia 的名词，所以这一对词的差别在词性，而不在来源。

normal.en: Patiently adds -ly to the adjective and describes the manner of bearing a delay.
normal.cn: patiently 给形容词加 -ly，描述承受延误的方式。

normal.en: Impatient adds im-, not, and names the refusal to keep bearing.
normal.cn: impatient 加上表示「不」的 im-，指不肯继续承受。

abstract.en: A word that names both the sick and the forbearing suggests that illness is the first school of patience.
abstract.cn: 一个词既指病人又指能忍耐的人，说明疾病是耐心的第一所学校。

abstract.en: Because the adjective and the noun share one shape, English lets a description of character stand for a person in a hospital bed.
abstract.cn: 因为形容词与名词共用一个形状，英语可以让对品性的描述直接指代病床上的人。

abstract.en: Patient care measures a system by how it treats people who can do nothing but wait.
abstract.cn: 病人护理衡量一个体系的方式，是看它如何对待那些除了等待什么也做不了的人。

examples.en: The patient waited quietly for his name to be called.
examples.cn: 那位病人安静地等着叫到他的名字。

examples.en: Please be patient with the new trainee.
examples.cn: 请对新来的实习生耐心一些。

examples.en: She stayed patient under a stream of rude questions.
examples.cn: 在一连串无礼的提问下，她仍然保持忍耐。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「陪身特」——亲人陪着身子特别弱的病人；记住 patient 是病人，也是「有耐心的」。

root: 拉丁语 pati（忍受）的现在分词 patiens 派生出 patient，既指「忍受着的（人）」，也指「病人」；同根的 patientia 则是名词 patience（耐心）的来源。patient 与 patience 同源，但 patient 主要作形容词「有耐心的」和名词「病人」，patience 只能作名词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is bearing something; the noun names the one who bears an illness, and the adjective names the one who bears delay or pressure.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是承受着某物；名词指承受疾病的人，形容词指承受延误或压力的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old man in a clinic corridor holding his folder, waiting for his name.
core.cn: 核心意象：诊所走廊里，一位老人抱着病历本，等着叫到自己的名字。

branches.en: a corridor of people holding folders
branches.cn: 走廊里抱着病历本的人们

branches.en: a nurse calling a name at a door
branches.cn: 护士在门口叫号

branches.en: a trainee told to try once more
branches.cn: 被告知再试一次的实习生

branches.en: a witness answering rude questions
branches.cn: 面对无礼提问的证人

branches.en: a bed beside a window in a ward
branches.cn: 病房里靠窗的一张床

intro.en: The word is a Latin participle reshaped by French, and English adds endings to build the adverb, the separate noun of the quality and the negative form.
intro.cn: 这个词是经法语改写的拉丁分词，英语再加词尾，造出副词、表示该品质的独立名词与否定形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin pati, patiens and patientia are all recorded, so patient has a documented ancestry shared with patience, patiently and impatient.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pati、patiens 与 patientia 均有记录，因此 patient 与 patience、patiently、impatient 共享有据可查的世系。

definition_zh: 图案；模式；规律；纸样；范例；（动词）仿照；以图案装饰
definition_en: a repeated design or a regular arrangement; a model to copy; also a verb meaning to model something on another or to decorate with a design
core_image: 一个方块被刻成印版，压到布上，再压一次、又一次，同样的形状排成一片
scene: 裁缝铺的长桌上摊开一张纸样，粉笔线在布面上勾出重复的方格，The tailor pins the paper pattern onto the cloth before cutting.
sceneCN: 这里 pattern 指「裁剪用的纸样模板」（第 3 个义项：供复制用的样板）；句意为裁缝把纸质样板别到布上再下剪。图中可辨识物件：长桌、纸样、粉笔线、别针与格纹布面；对应第 1 个义项。

derivatives.zh: 有图案的；按模式排列的
图案形成；模式化

senses.title: A repeated decorative design
senses.definition: a design of repeated shapes, lines or colours used to decorate a surface
senses.definitionCN: 由重复的形状、线条或色彩构成、用于装饰表面的图样
senses.example: The curtains carry a small floral pattern.
senses.exampleCN: 窗帘上带着细小的花卉图案。
senses.why: The word began as patron, 'a model to copy'; decoration repeats a copied unit across a surface.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初借自意为「可复制的范本」的外来词；装饰正是把一个被复制的单元铺满表面。

senses.title: A recurring sequence of events
senses.definition: a regular and repeated way in which events or actions occur
senses.definitionCN: 事件或行为有规律地反复出现的方式
senses.example: The patient's sleep pattern changed after the journey.
senses.exampleCN: 旅行之后，这位患者的睡眠规律变了。
senses.why: Once a model is repeated in time rather than on a surface, the repetition itself becomes the pattern.
senses.whyCN: 当范本不是铺在表面、而是在时间中反复，重复本身就成了模式。

senses.title: A template or model for making copies
senses.titleCN: 供复制使用的样板或模板
senses.definition: a shape or model used as a guide for cutting, sewing or casting
senses.definitionCN: 裁剪、缝制或浇铸时用作依据的形状或模型
senses.example: She pinned the paper pattern to the fabric and cut along the chalk line.
senses.exampleCN: 她把纸质样板别到布上，沿粉笔线剪开。
senses.why: This is the literal ancestor: a pattern is first an object you lay down and copy.
senses.whyCN: 这是字面上的祖先义：pattern 最初就是一件可以铺下来照着复制的东西。

senses.title: The arrangement of parts that forms a whole
senses.definition: the way elements are arranged or organized in a whole
senses.definitionCN: 各要素在整体中被排列或组织的方式
senses.example: The novel's pattern of images returns in the last chapter.
senses.exampleCN: 小说中那组意象的排列在最后一章再次出现。
senses.why: From a copied outline the sense broadens to any arrangement whose parts answer one another.
senses.whyCN: 从可复制的轮廓出发，词义扩展到任何部件彼此呼应的排列。

senses.title: A regularity detected in data or nature
senses.titleCN: 在数据或自然中找出的规律
senses.definition: a recognizable regularity in measurements, behaviour or natural forms
senses.definitionCN: 在测量、行为或自然形态中可辨认的规律性
senses.example: The software looks for patterns in the sales figures.
senses.exampleCN: 软件在销售数据中寻找规律。
senses.why: Science makes the repetition an object of search: the pattern is the order found in what looked random.
senses.whyCN: 科学把重复变成搜寻的对象：模式就是从看似随机之物里找出的秩序。

senses.title: A recurring arrangement in language
senses.titleCN: 语言中反复出现的结构
senses.definition: a regular arrangement of sounds or words that speakers of a language follow
senses.definitionCN: 说某种语言的人所遵循的、语音或词句的规律性排列
senses.example: The drill fixes the sentence pattern in memory.
senses.exampleCN: 反复操练把句型固定在记忆里。
senses.why: Language is learned through repeated shapes, so the same word names the frames a speaker reuses.
senses.whyCN: 语言通过反复的形状被学会，同一个词便用来命名说话者反复套用的框架。

senses.title: A model of conduct held up for imitation
senses.definition: an example or model of behaviour that others are expected to follow
senses.definitionCN: 他人应当效仿的行为榜样或范例
senses.example: The older teachers were held up as a pattern of patience.
senses.exampleCN: 那些年长的教师被举为耐心的典范。
senses.why: This restores the Latin model sense: patronus was a protector and an exemplar, and pattern kept that moral use into modern English.
senses.whyCN: 这恢复了拉丁语的范本义：patronus 既是保护人也是榜样，pattern 把这一道德用法保留到现代英语。

senses.title: To model something on, or decorate with a design
senses.definition: to make or shape something according to a model, or to decorate a surface with a regular design
senses.definitionCN: 依照某个范本制作或塑造某物，或以规则图样装饰表面
senses.example: The garden was patterned on a larger estate in the north.
senses.exampleCN: 这座花园是仿照北方一处更大的庄园建造的。
senses.why: The verb turns the noun into an action: whatever follows a model is patterned on it, and a surface given a repeated design is patterned too.
senses.whyCN: 动词把名词变成动作：照着范本做的，就是依范本而制；被赋予重复图样的表面也可说带图样的。

intro.en: Pattern comes from Middle English patron, taken from Latin patronus 'protector, model', which was built on pater 'father'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: pattern 来自中古英语的借形，后者出自拉丁语 patronus「保护人、范本」，而 patronus 由 pater「父亲」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Pater meant 'father'. It is the base of patronus and also of English words about fatherhood and protection.
items.cn: pater 意为「父亲」。它既是 patronus 的词基，也是一批表示父系与保护的英语词的来源。

items.en: The suffix -onus built nouns of role or function; added to pater it produced patronus, 'one who acts as a father to others'.
items.cn: 后缀 -onus 构成表示角色或职能的名词；加在 pater 上便产生 patronus，意为「替他人承担父职的人」。

items.en: Patronus meant 'protector, defender' and, in later Latin, 'a model or example to be followed'.
items.cn: patronus 意为「保护人、辩护者」，在后期拉丁语中又指「可供效法的范本或榜样」。

items.en: English took patron through Old French, where it kept both the protector and the model senses.
items.cn: 英语经由古法语接受这个借形，古法语同时保留了保护人与范本两种含义。

items.en: In Middle English the spelling shifted from patron to pattern, and the 'model' sense moved to the centre of the word.
items.cn: 在中古英语中，拼写最终定为 pattern，「范本」义逐渐成为这个词的核心。

items.en: Source uncertain: why the written form settled as pattern rather than patron is not fully explained; sixteenth-century spelling habits are generally assumed to be the cause.
items.cn: 来源不确定：书写形式为何最终定为 pattern 而非较早的借形，尚无完满解释；一般认为与 16 世纪的拼写习惯有关。

note.en: The first group holds words that look close to pattern, including its own ancestor; the second holds words for design and for models to copy, which differ in what they stress.
note.cn: 第一组是外形接近 pattern 的词，其中包含它自己的祖先形式；第二组指图案与可复制的范本，各自强调的方面不同。

entries.definition: A person who supports or protects someone; this is the form English borrowed first, before pattern took over the model sense.
entries.definitionCN: 支持或保护他人的人；这是英语最先借入的形式，后来 pattern 才承担了范本义。

entries.definition: An official right to an invention; from Latin patere 'to lie open', with no link to pater 'father'.
entries.definitionCN: 对发明享有的官方专有权；来自拉丁语 patere「敞开」，与 pater「父亲」无关。

entries.definition: A wooden shoe or clog worn to raise the foot above mud; it only sounds like pattern and has no shared sense with it.
entries.definitionCN: 垫高脚步以免陷入泥中的木鞋或木套鞋；只是读音像 pattern，意义并无交集。

entries.definition: The planned arrangement of lines, shapes or colours; design can be invented rather than repeated, while pattern stresses repetition.
entries.definitionCN: 对线条、形状或色彩的规划性安排；设计可以原创而不必重复，pattern 则强调重复。

entries.definition: One repeated figure within a design; a motif is the unit that a pattern repeats.
entries.definitionCN: 图案中反复出现的单个图形；母题正是被图案重复的那个单元。

entries.definition: A shaped guide for cutting or drawing; it is the physical model sense of pattern, without the decorative senses.
entries.definitionCN: 裁剪或描画用的成形样板；它就是 pattern 的实体范本义，不含装饰性的义项。

entries.definition: A thing or person taken as an example to copy; model is wider and also covers scale models and abstract systems.
entries.definitionCN: 被拿来照着做的物或人；model 范围更广，还包括缩比模型与抽象系统。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin pieces, the real word family and the phrases the word actually keeps.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁构件、真实的同族词，以及这个词实际常用的搭配。

normal.en: Pattern began as patron, a model to copy.
normal.cn: pattern 最初借自一个意为「可照抄的范本」的外来词。

normal.en: A pattern repeats one unit across a surface, like a stamp pressed again and again.
normal.cn: 图案是把一个单元铺满表面，像印章一次次压下去。

normal.en: The paper pattern in a sewing shop is a model laid on cloth.
normal.cn: 裁缝铺里的纸质样板，就是铺在布上的模型。

normal.en: Weather patterns repeat in time, not on a wall.
normal.cn: 天气模式在时间中重复，而不是在墙上重复。

normal.en: Pattern recognition is the search for order in what first looks random.
normal.cn: 模式识别就是在初看杂乱之处寻找秩序。

abstract.en: Picture a single tile copied until the whole floor becomes a story.
abstract.cn: 想象一块瓷砖被不断复制，直到整个地面成为一个故事。

abstract.en: Picture a river that cuts the same bend every year.
abstract.cn: 想象一条河每年都切出同一个弯。

abstract.en: Picture a sentence frame that many different words can step into.
abstract.cn: 想象一个句子框架，许多不同的词都能走进去。

examples.en: The tiles form a geometric pattern across the floor.
examples.cn: 瓷砖在地面上构成几何图案。

examples.en: Doctors noticed a pattern in the patients' symptoms.
examples.cn: 医生们注意到患者的症状中有一种规律。

examples.en: The new school was patterned on a design from the coast.
examples.cn: 这所新学校是仿照沿海地区的一个设计建造的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「派藤」——藤条编出的格子一遍遍重复，派上去铺满就成图案。patron 本是「范本」，照着范本一次次复制，就有了 pattern。

root: 中古英语的借形来自拉丁语 patronus「保护人、范本」；patronus 由 pater「父亲」加名词后缀 -onus 构成。拼写后来变为 pattern，「范本、样板」义成为核心，再引申出图案、模式与规律等义。拼写变化的具体原因属假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with a repeated decorative design, then move to a sequence in time and a model cut from paper, to arrangement and detected regularity, to language and moral example, and end with the verb.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从重复的装饰图案开始，转到时间中的次序与纸质样板，再到部件排列与被找出的规律，再到语言结构与道德典范，最后是动词用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one unit is stamped, cut or copied again and again, so repetition itself becomes the visible order.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个单元被反复压印、裁剪或复制，重复本身成了可见的秩序。

branches.en: THE REPEATED UNIT: the core sense is a copied shape repeated across a surface until the surface is covered.
branches.cn: 重复的单元：核心义是一个被复制的形状在表面上反复出现，直到铺满。

branches.en: REPETITION IN TIME OR ON PAPER: a habit repeats on a schedule, and a template is the model laid down before the copy is made.
branches.cn: 在时间中或在纸上的重复：习惯按时间表反复，样板则是复制之前铺下的模型。

branches.en: ARRANGEMENT AND ORDER: the word widens from a visible design to the way parts fit a whole, and then to a regularity found in data.
branches.cn: 排列与秩序：词义从可见图样扩展到部件构成整体的方式，再扩展到数据中被找出的规律。

branches.en: A SHAPE OTHERS COPY: a sentence frame is reused by speakers, and a moral example is held up for others to follow.
branches.cn: 被别人复制的形状：句型被说话者反复套用，道德榜样则被举出来供人效法。

branches.en: THE ACTION OF COPYING: the noun becomes a verb, so a thing can be patterned on a model or patterned with a design.
branches.cn: 复制的动作：名词转为动词，于是可以说某物仿照某个范本，或表面被赋予图样。

intro.en: Pattern can be read as a Latin noun base, a Latin role suffix and the English word that grew out of them, plus two adjective endings.
intro.cn: pattern 可以读作一个拉丁名词词基、一个拉丁角色后缀、由它们生长出来的英语词，再加两个形容词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin pater 'father' with -onus produced patronus 'protector, model'; English shortened it to patron, respelled it pattern, and later added -ed and -less.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pater「父亲」加 -onus 构成 patronus「保护人、范本」；英语先缩略这个词形，再改写为 pattern，后来又加两个词尾构成形容词。

items.example: The noun supplies the family image behind the Latin word.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词提供拉丁词背后的家族意象。

items.meaning: one who acts in a role or function
items.meaningCN: 承担某种角色或职能的人
items.example: The suffix turns 'father' into a word for one who protects others.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把「父亲」变成表示保护他人者之词。

items.example: Latin used the noun for a protector and later for an example.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语用这个名词指保护人，后来也指榜样。

items.example: English kept the older form beside its respelled doublet.
items.exampleCN: 英语把较旧的形式与改写后的同源词并存在一起。

items.structure: pattern (English noun and verb, respelled from patron)
items.meaning: a repeated design; a model to copy
items.meaningCN: 重复的图案；可复制的范本
items.example: The respelled form took over the model and design senses.
items.exampleCN: 改写后的形式承接了范本与图案两种含义。

items.example: The suffix builds the adjective of possession.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成表示拥有的形容词。

items.meaning: having a pattern; modelled on something
items.example: The fabric is patterned with small squares.
items.exampleCN: 这块布上有小方格图案。

items.example: The suffix removes the quality the noun names.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀去掉名词所指的性质。

derivatives.meaning: the noun of design shifts to an adjective meaning 'provided with a pattern' or 'modelled on something'
derivatives.meaningCN: 由表示图案的名词转为形容词，表示「带有图案」或「仿照某物」

derivatives.meaning: the noun shifts to an adjective meaning 'having no pattern'
derivatives.meaningCN: 由名词转为形容词，表示「没有图案的」

definition_zh: 暂停；停顿；间歇；迟疑
definition_en: to stop doing something for a short time and then continue; also a short stop in speech, music or action
core_image: 悬在半空的手指：动作停住，却没有结束
scene: 录音棚里，主持人的话说到一半，抬眼看了看稿子。The host paused in the middle of the sentence to check the script.
sceneCN: 这里是「暂停、停顿」（第 1 个义项：短暂停下再继续）；句意为主持人说到一半停下来看稿子。图中可辨识物件：话筒、稿纸、亮着的录音灯。

derivatives.zh: 由 pause 加 -ing 构成，指停顿这个动作或停住的那段时间
由 pause 与 button 复合而成，指画着两条竖线的暂停键
由拉丁词干 paus- 加 -al 构成，语音学中指「停顿处的」

senses.title: To stop for a short time
senses.definition: to stop what you are doing for a short time and then continue
senses.definitionCN: 把正在做的事短时间停下，随后继续
senses.example: The host paused in the middle of the sentence to check the script.
senses.exampleCN: 主持人说到一半停下来看稿子。
senses.why: The Greek verb pauein meant to make something stop, and English keeps that plain sense of a break that does not end the action.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语动词 pauein 意为「使停止」，英语保留了这层朴素含义：停一下，但动作并没有结束。

senses.title: A short stop in an activity
senses.definition: a short period in which an activity or a flow of speech stops
senses.definitionCN: 活动或说话流程短暂中断的那一小段时间
senses.example: After a short pause, the music started again.
senses.exampleCN: 短暂停顿之后，音乐又响起来。
senses.why: Once the verb names the act of stopping, the same form can name the gap itself, so the action becomes a measurable interval.
senses.whyCN: 动词既然能指「停」这个动作，同一个词形也能指停出来的那段空隙，动作于是变成可以计量的间歇。

senses.title: A sign holding a note longer
senses.definition: a written sign telling a performer to hold a note or rest longer than its written value
senses.definitionCN: 乐谱上要求演奏者把某个音或休止延长到超出时值的记号
senses.example: The conductor placed a pause over the final chord.
senses.exampleCN: 指挥在最后一个和弦上方标了延长记号。
senses.why: In music the idea of a deliberate hold is written down as a sign, so the word moves from a moment of time to a mark on the page.
senses.whyCN: 在音乐里，「有意停住」被写成谱面上的记号，这个词便从一段时间落到纸上的一个符号。

senses.title: To hesitate before acting
senses.definition: to wait a moment before speaking or acting because you are not sure
senses.definitionCN: 因为拿不准，在开口或行动之前先等一等
senses.example: She paused before she answered the question.
senses.exampleCN: 她回答问题之前迟疑了一下。
senses.why: A pause can be caused by doubt rather than by rest, and that hesitation is the same bodily stillness seen from the inside.
senses.whyCN: 停顿有时不是因为休息，而是因为心里拿不准；这种犹豫就是同一种身体静止，只是从内心去看它。

intro.en: Pause comes from Greek and Latin words for stopping and reached English through Old French before it was applied to music, buttons and hesitation.
intro.cn: pause 源自希腊语与拉丁语中表示「停止」的词，经古法语进入英语，后来又用于音乐、按键与犹豫。

items.en: The noun pausis meant a stopping or a rest, and it came from the verb pauein, to make something cease.
items.cn: 名词 pausis 意为停止、歇息，来自动词 pauein，即「使某事物停下」。

items.en: Latin took the Greek noun as pausa, a halt or a rest, and used it for a break in speech and in work.
items.cn: 拉丁语把希腊语名词借作 pausa，意为中止、休息，用于说话与劳作中的间歇。

items.en: Old French kept the form pause with the same sense of a stop or a rest and passed it across the Channel.
items.cn: 古法语保留 pause 这一形式，仍指停下或休息，并把它传过海峡。

items.en: Middle English pause is recorded from the fifteenth century, first in religious and learned writing, then in ordinary description of speech.
items.cn: 中古英语的 pause 自十五世纪有记录，先见于宗教与学术文字，后来用于描述日常说话。

items.en: Modern English extends pause to a printed music sign, to the button that freezes a recording, and to the hesitation before a difficult answer.
items.cn: 现代英语把 pause 扩展到乐谱记号、让录音停住的按键，以及面对难题回答前的迟疑。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the Latin and French relatives plus two words that only share the spelling or the sound; the near-meaning group gathers words for stopping and for the gap itself.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁语与法语同族词，另加两个只是拼写或读音相近的词；近义组收表示停止与表示那段空隙的词。

entries.definition: The Latin noun for a halt or a rest, the source of the English word.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语名词，意为中止或休息，是英语这个词的来源。

entries.definition: Rest or quiet, built in Latin on the same root for pausing.
entries.definitionCN: 休息、安静，在拉丁语中建立在同一个表示停顿的词根上。

entries.definition: To place the body in a position, from a different Latin verb; only the spelling looks close.
entries.definitionCN: 摆出姿势，来自另一个拉丁语动词；只是拼写看上去接近，词源不同。

entries.definition: The plural of paw, an animal foot; it sounds the same but is a different word.
entries.definitionCN: paw 的复数，指动物的脚掌；读音相同，却是另一个词。

entries.definition: To end movement or action, usually for longer than a pause.
entries.definitionCN: 结束运动或动作，通常比停顿更久。

entries.definition: To stop moving, or to bring something to a stop.
entries.definitionCN: 停止移动，或使某事物停下。

entries.definition: A short period when an activity stops before it starts again.
entries.definitionCN: 活动暂停、之后重新开始的那段短时间。

entries.definition: A period of time between two events or between parts of a performance.
entries.definitionCN: 两个事件之间或演出两部分之间的时间。

normalIntro.en: The word carries a Greek verb of stopping through Latin and French, and its English life is a chain of short holds: breath, music, button, doubt.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词把希腊语中表示「使停止」的动词经拉丁语和法语带进英语，它在英语里的经历是一连串短暂的停住：喘息、音乐、按键、犹豫。

normal.en: Greek pauein meant to make something stop, and pausis was the halt that came of it.
normal.cn: 希腊语 pauein 意为使某事物停下，pausis 就是由此产生的停止。

normal.en: Latin pausa and Old French pause keep almost the same shape, so the spelling barely moved on the way into English.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 pausa 与古法语 pause 形式几乎不变，所以进入英语时拼写几乎没有挪动。

normal.en: Pause for breath is the oldest kind of pause: the body cuts speech short in order to breathe.
normal.cn: pause for breath 是最古老的一种停顿：身体为了让说话中断去喘口气。

normal.en: Press pause points at the two upright bars on a player, a small picture of an action held still.
normal.cn: press pause 指播放器上那两条竖线，是把动作按住的一小幅图画。

normal.en: The verb drops the final e before -ing, so pause becomes pausing, not pauseing.
normal.cn: 动词加 -ing 时去掉词尾的 e，所以写成 pausing，而不是 pauseing。

abstract.en: A pause is proof that stopping and continuing are not opposites: the same action contains both.
abstract.cn: 停顿证明「停」与「继续」并不对立：同一个动作里两者都在。

abstract.en: Silence held for a moment can carry more weight than the words on either side of it.
abstract.cn: 被刻意留住的一小段沉默，往往比它两边的字句更有分量。

abstract.en: Every pause button assumes that what is frozen will come back, which is why the word sounds calm rather than final.
abstract.cn: 每个暂停键都预设被冻住的东西还会回来，所以这个词听起来平静，而不像终结。

examples.en: The host paused in the middle of the sentence to check the script.
examples.cn: 主持人说到一半停下来看稿子。

examples.en: There was a long pause before anyone spoke.
examples.cn: 好一阵停顿之后才有人开口。

examples.en: Pause the video when the diagram appears.
examples.cn: 图出现的时候把视频暂停一下。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泡子」——水快开时先冒一阵泡子，火候不到就再等等；pause 就是中途停一下。

root: 希腊语 pauein（使停止）→ 希腊语 pausis（停止）→ 拉丁语 pausa（中止、休息）→ 古法语 pause → 英语 pause；同族词多与「停、歇」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a short hold that leaves the action open; from it come the gap in time, the written music sign, and the hesitation of doubt.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心意象是「停住但没结束」；由此分出时间上的空隙、谱面上的延长记号，以及因拿不准而产生的迟疑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger frozen above a button, the action held but not finished.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根手指停在按键上方，动作被按住却没有结束。

branches.en: a speaker stopping mid-sentence
branches.cn: 说话的人在半句上停住

branches.en: the empty second after a question
branches.cn: 一个问题之后空出来的那一秒

branches.en: a printed sign above the last chord
branches.cn: 最后一个和弦上方的谱面记号

branches.en: a hand raised before an answer
branches.cn: 回答之前抬起的手

branches.en: the same stillness read once as time and once as doubt
branches.cn: 同一种静止，一处读作时间，一处读作犹豫

intro.en: A Greek root for stopping runs through the Greek noun, the Latin noun and verb, the French form, and two English endings that build new words from it.
intro.cn: 表示「停止」的希腊词根贯穿希腊语名词、拉丁语名词与动词、法语形式，以及两个由它造词的英语后缀。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 爪子；脚掌；用手抓摸
definition_en: the foot of an animal that has claws, especially a cat or dog; also to touch or scrape something with such a foot
core_image: 一只毛茸茸的脚掌落下，爪尖在触地前才微微伸出
scene: 清晨的厨房门外，一只橘猫蹲在垫子上，盯着关紧的门。The cat lifted one paw and tapped the wood.
sceneCN: 这里是「爪子」（第 1 个义项：动物的脚掌）；句意为猫抬起一只爪子去拍木门。图中可辨识物件：橘猫、门缝、门口的地垫。

derivatives.zh: 由 paw 与 print 复合而成，指动物踩在软地面上留下的爪印
由 paw 加 -ing 构成的动名词，指用爪子反复抓扒的动作

senses.title: The foot of a clawed animal
senses.definition: the foot of an animal such as a cat or dog, with soft pads and claws
senses.definitionCN: 猫、狗等动物带软垫和爪尖的脚掌
senses.example: The cat lifted one paw and tapped the wood.
senses.exampleCN: 猫抬起一只爪子拍了拍木门。
senses.why: The word names the whole padded foot rather than a single claw, which is why it covers the part that walks and the part that grips.
senses.whyCN: 这个词指整只带肉垫的脚掌，而不是单根爪尖，所以既能说走路的那部分，也能说抓握的那部分。

senses.title: A person's hand, informally
senses.definition: a person's hand, used in informal speech, often when the hand is clumsy or intrusive
senses.definitionCN: 口语里指人的手，常带笨拙或乱伸的意味
senses.example: Keep your paws off my notes.
senses.exampleCN: 别用你的手碰我的笔记。
senses.why: Calling a hand a paw borrows the animal foot to suggest clumsiness or greed, so the same word slides from beast to person.
senses.whyCN: 把人的手叫作爪子，是借动物的脚掌暗示笨拙或贪心，于是同一个词从兽类滑到人身上。

senses.title: To scrape with a paw
senses.definition: to touch, scrape or hit something repeatedly with a paw
senses.definitionCN: 用爪子反复触碰、刮擦或拍打某物
senses.example: The dog pawed at the door until someone opened it.
senses.exampleCN: 狗一直扒门，直到有人把它打开。
senses.why: From the noun for the foot comes a verb for what that foot does, and the repeated scraping is the action most often attached to it.
senses.whyCN: 名词指脚掌，动词就指这只脚做的事，而最常与它相连的动作就是反复刮擦。

senses.title: To touch someone roughly
senses.definition: to touch a person in a rough or unwanted way, especially with the hands
senses.definitionCN: 用手粗鲁地或不被欢迎地触碰别人
senses.example: He pawed at her sleeve to get her attention.
senses.exampleCN: 他粗鲁地扯她的袖子想引起注意。
senses.why: Because a paw is clumsy and has no fine control, the verb came to describe hands that grab without care, and the meaning turns negative.
senses.whyCN: 爪子笨拙、没有细致控制，动词便用来形容不加分寸乱抓的手，含义也转向负面。

intro.en: The word for an animal foot appears in Middle English, and the usual account traces it to an Old French form; anything earlier is uncertain.
intro.cn: 表示动物脚掌的这个词见于中古英语，通常认为来自古法语的一种形式；再往前的情况并不确定。

items.en: Old French patte meant the foot or paw of an animal, and it is generally taken as the source of the English word.
items.cn: 古法语 patte 意为动物的脚或爪子，一般认为这就是英语这个词的来源。

items.en: Some scholars connect it with Germanic words for a foot, perhaps through Frankish, but this remains a reconstructed and disputed suggestion.
items.cn: 一些学者把它与日耳曼语中表示「脚」的词联系起来，可能经由法兰克语，但这仍属于重构且有争议的推测。

items.en: Middle English records pawe in the fourteenth century, spelled with a w that later settled into the modern form.
items.cn: 中古英语在十四世纪记录了 pawe 这一写法，词尾的 w 后来固定成现代形式。

items.en: Early modern writers extended the noun to a person's hand in rough or joking speech, and the verb for scraping followed.
items.cn: 近代早期作家在粗俗或玩笑的语气里把这个名词扩展到人的手，表示抓扒的动词也随之出现。

items.en: Modern English keeps both the animal sense and the informal human sense, and forms compounds such as pawprint for the mark left behind.
items.cn: 现代英语同时保留动物义与口语中的人手义，并造出 pawprint 这类复合词，指留下的印记。

note.en: The look-alike group holds compounds and inflections of the word plus one short word that merely shares its ending; the near-meaning group holds other words for feet and for grasping.
note.cn: 形近组收这个词的复合形式与变形，以及一个只是词尾相同的短词；近义组收其他表示脚掌与抓握的词。

entries.definition: The mark a paw leaves on soft ground or on a dusty floor.
entries.definitionCN: 爪子在软地或落灰的地面上留下的印记。

entries.definition: The plural of the noun and the third person singular of the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 名词复数，也是动词的第三人称单数形式。

entries.definition: A bone of the mouth used for biting; only the ending looks alike, the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 嘴里用来咬东西的骨；只是词尾相像，词源不同。

entries.definition: A sharp curved nail on the foot of a bird or animal.
entries.definitionCN: 鸟或动物脚上弯曲而锋利的甲。

entries.definition: The soft part on the underside of an animal's foot.
entries.definitionCN: 动物脚掌下面柔软的肉垫部分。

entries.definition: The hard horny foot of a horse, cow or similar animal.
entries.definitionCN: 马、牛等动物坚硬而角质化的脚。

entries.definition: The part of the body at the end of the arm, with fingers.
entries.definitionCN: 手臂末端带手指的部分。

normalIntro.en: With no reliable Latin root, the word is best held by its French source, its English spellings, and the small family built from it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁词根，最好靠它的法语来源、英语拼写，以及由它组成的小词族来记。

normal.en: Old French patte meant an animal's foot, and English took the shape of that word as paw.
normal.cn: 古法语 patte 意为动物的脚，英语照这个词的形状收下了 paw。

normal.en: Add s and you get paws, which is both the plural noun and the third person singular verb.
normal.cn: 加上 s 成为 paws，既是名词复数，也是动词的第三人称单数。

normal.en: Paw at the door describes the scraping motion a cat makes when it wants to be let in.
normal.cn: paw at the door 描写猫想进屋时用爪子刮门的样子。

normal.en: Pawprint joins paw and print, so the mark is literally the print of a paw.
normal.cn: pawprint 把 paw 与 print 拼在一起，那印记字面上就是爪子的印。

normal.en: A cat's paw in a story is a person used by someone else to do a risky job.
normal.cn: 故事里的 cat's paw 指被人利用去干冒险差事的人。

abstract.en: A paw is a foot that still remembers hunting, which is why the same word can mean standing and grabbing.
abstract.cn: 爪子是一只还记得捕猎的脚，所以同一个词既能表示站立，也能表示抓取。

abstract.en: Calling a human hand a paw is a small insult: it says the hand has lost its delicacy.
abstract.cn: 把人的手叫作爪子是一句小小的贬损：它在说这只手已经失去了细致。

abstract.en: The soft pad under the animal's foot is a cushion that also hides the claws until they are needed.
abstract.cn: 动物脚掌下那块软垫既是缓冲，也把爪尖藏到需要时才亮出来。

examples.en: The cat lifted one paw and tapped the wood.
examples.cn: 猫抬起一只爪子拍了拍木门。

examples.en: Muddy paw prints covered the kitchen floor.
examples.cn: 泥爪印布满了厨房地面。

examples.en: The dog pawed at the door until someone opened it.
examples.cn: 狗一直扒门，直到有人把它打开。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「刨」——猫用爪子在门上刨来刨去；paw 就是爪子，也是用爪抓。

root: 一般认为来自古法语 patte（动物的脚、爪）；更早来源不确定，有学者把它与日耳曼语中表示「脚」的词相联系，属重构假说；无可靠拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a soft padded foot that both carries the body and scrapes at what it wants; the human and rough-touching senses grow from that same clumsiness.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是既能承重、又会抓扒的带垫脚掌；指人手与粗鲁触碰的两个义项，都从这种笨拙里长出来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a soft padded foot pressing down, claws folded until the moment they are needed.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只带肉垫的脚掌按下去，爪尖折着，等到需要时才伸出。

branches.en: a cat waiting at a closed door
branches.cn: 一只猫等在关着的门边

branches.en: a hand pushed away from a desk
branches.cn: 一只手被人从桌边挡开

branches.en: claws working at wood until it gives
branches.cn: 爪尖一直刮到木头松动

branches.en: a sleeve pulled without asking
branches.cn: 没有打招呼就扯住的袖子

branches.en: the same foot that stands also scratches
branches.cn: 同一只脚既站着，也用来抓扒

intro.en: This word has no reliable Latin root, so its build is held by the Old French form, two English spellings, and the compounding and suffixing that follow.
intro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁词根，构词线索由古法语形式、两个英语拼写，以及随后的复合与加缀组成。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word; the trail stops at Old French and possibly a Germanic source.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词：线索止于古法语，再往前可能是某种日耳曼语来源。

definition_zh: 支付；付钱；值得；薪水
definition_en: to give money in return for goods or work; also to bring a good result, and the money received for a job
core_image: 一只手把钱推过柜台，另一只手把东西递回来
scene: 深夜的小餐馆里，服务员把账单放在桌角。He paid the bill and left a tip under the cup.
sceneCN: 这里是「支付、付钱」（第 1 个义项：为商品或服务付款）；句意为他付了账单，还把零钱压在杯子下面。图中可辨识物件：账单夹、咖啡杯、收银台的小灯。

derivatives.zh: 由 pay 加名词后缀 -ment 构成，指付款这一行为或付出的款项
由 pay 加 -able 构成，指应付的、可支付的
由 pay 加表示「做某事的人」的 -er 构成，指付款人
由 pay 加表示「受事者」的 -ee 构成，指收款人

senses.title: To give money for something
senses.definition: to give someone money in return for goods, work or a service
senses.definitionCN: 为货物、劳动或服务把钱交给对方
senses.example: She paid for the tickets with her phone.
senses.exampleCN: 她用手机付了票钱。
senses.why: The Latin root meant to pacify, and handing over money was seen as calming the person who was owed, so payment began as an act of settling.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为「使平静」，把钱交出去被看作让被欠的一方平静下来，所以付款最初是一种平息。

senses.title: To be worth the effort
senses.definition: to bring a benefit that is worth the cost or effort involved
senses.definitionCN: 带来足以抵过所付代价或力气的好处
senses.example: It pays to read the instructions first.
senses.exampleCN: 先读说明是值得的。
senses.why: If money paid can settle a debt, then any effort can be said to pay when it returns something worth more than it cost.
senses.whyCN: 既然付出的钱可以结清债务，那么任何力气只要能换回超过代价的东西，也可以说它 pay。

senses.title: Money received for work
senses.definition: the money that someone receives for the work they do
senses.definitionCN: 因工作而得到的报酬
senses.example: The pay is low, but the hours are short.
senses.exampleCN: 工资不高，但工时短。
senses.why: The verb names the act of handing money over; turned into a noun, it names the money that arrives on the other side of the same exchange.
senses.whyCN: 动词指把钱交出去的动作；变成名词后，它指同一场交换里流到另一边的钱。

senses.title: To suffer a cost
senses.definition: to experience something unpleasant as a result of what one has done
senses.definitionCN: 因自己做过的事而承受不愉快的后果
senses.example: He paid dearly for that careless remark.
senses.exampleCN: 他为那句轻率的话付出了很大代价。
senses.why: Once pay means to give up something for a result, the thing given up need not be money, so a mistake can be paid for with pain or time.
senses.whyCN: 当 pay 表示为了结果交出东西，交出的就不必是钱，于是错误也可以用痛苦或时间来偿还。

intro.en: Pay goes back to a Latin word for peace, and it reached English through French with the practical sense of settling what is owed.
intro.cn: pay 可以追溯到拉丁语中表示和平的词，经法语进入英语时带上了「结清所欠」的实际含义。

items.en: Pax meant peace, and a dispute that had been settled was imagined as quiet after conflict.
items.cn: pax 意为和平，被平息下来的争端被想象成冲突之后的安静。

items.en: The verb pacare meant to make peaceful or to quiet someone, and it could describe calming an angry creditor.
items.cn: 动词 pacare 意为使平静、安抚某人，也可以形容安抚愤怒的债主。

items.en: In medieval Latin the verb took the practical sense of satisfying a debt, so money quieted a person the way peace quieted a quarrel.
items.cn: 在中世纪拉丁语里，这个动词获得了「清偿债务」的实际含义：钱让人平息，正如和平让争吵平息。

items.en: Old French payer carried that sense of satisfying someone with money, and Anglo-French carried it into law and trade.
items.cn: 古法语 payer 承下用钱让人满足的含义，盎格鲁法语又把它带进法律与商业。

items.en: Middle English payen becomes modern pay, with the irregular past paid, and the noun pay for the money earned.
items.cn: 中古英语 payen 变成现代 pay，过去式是不规则的 paid，名词 pay 则指挣到的钱。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers inflections, derivatives and Latin relatives of the word; the near-meaning group gathers verbs for settling a debt and nouns for what work earns.
note.cn: 形近组收这个词的变形、派生词与拉丁同族词；近义组收表示结清债务的动词和表示劳动所得的名词。

entries.definition: The past tense and past participle of pay, formed without the regular -ed ending.
entries.definitionCN: pay 的过去式与过去分词，没有按常规加 -ed。

entries.definition: A person or organization that pays money.
entries.definitionCN: 付钱的人或机构。

entries.definition: To make someone calm or quiet, from the same Latin verb as pay.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人平静下来，与 pay 同出拉丁语动词。

entries.definition: The state of quiet and freedom from conflict that the Latin root named.
entries.definitionCN: 那个拉丁词根所指的安宁、无冲突状态。

entries.definition: To pay what is owed and so close an account.
entries.definitionCN: 付清欠款从而结清账目。

entries.definition: Money paid to a worker, usually by the hour or the day.
entries.definitionCN: 付给工人的报酬，通常按小时或按天计。

entries.definition: A fixed amount paid to an employee each month or year.
entries.definitionCN: 按月或按年付给雇员的固定报酬。

entries.definition: Money paid for a service or for the right to do something.
entries.definitionCN: 为某项服务或某项权利付出的费用。

normalIntro.en: The word grows out of a Latin noun for peace, and its history is the story of turning money into quiet.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从拉丁语中表示和平的名词长出来，它的历史就是把钱变成安静的过程。

normal.en: The Latin word for peace is pax, and it is the seed of pay: to pay was to make a creditor peaceful.
normal.cn: 表示和平的拉丁词是 pax，它就是 pay 的种子：付钱原本是让债主平静下来。

normal.en: Pacare means to quiet someone, so payment is a kind of calming carried out with money.
normal.cn: pacare 意为使人平静，所以付款是一种用钱完成的安抚。

normal.en: The past tense is paid, not payed, because the word came through French instead of being built inside English.
normal.cn: 过去式是 paid 而不是 payed，因为它经法语传来，不是英语自己造的。

normal.en: Pay attention uses the same verb for giving something invisible: you hand over your notice.
normal.cn: pay attention 用同一个动词表示给出无形的东西：你把注意力交出去。

normal.en: A payer sends money and a payee receives it, so the suffixes -er and -ee point in opposite directions.
normal.cn: payer 付钱，payee 收钱，后缀 -er 与 -ee 的方向正好相反。

abstract.en: Every payment begins as a promise, which is why the root of the word means peace rather than money.
abstract.cn: 每一笔付款最初都是一个承诺，所以这个词的词根表示和平，而不是钱。

abstract.en: The word treats a debt as a small quarrel that money can quiet.
abstract.cn: 这个词把债务看成一场小争吵，钱可以让它安静下来。

abstract.en: Pay is the point where effort and reward are weighed against each other on the same scale.
abstract.cn: pay 是力气与回报被放在同一杆秤上互相衡量的那个点。

examples.en: She paid for the tickets with her phone.
examples.cn: 她用手机付了票钱。

examples.en: It pays to read the instructions first.
examples.cn: 先读说明是值得的。

examples.en: The pay is low, but the hours are short.
examples.cn: 工资不高，但工时短。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「赔」——把钱付出去，像赔给别人一样；pay 就是支付。

root: 拉丁语 pax（和平）→ pacare（使平静、清偿）→ 中世纪拉丁语「偿还债主」→ 古法语 payer → 英语 pay；同族词多与「平息、付清」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is handing over money to quiet a claim; from that act come the sense of worth, the noun for wages, and the wider cost paid for a mistake.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是把钱交出去让索求平息；由这个动作分出「值得」、表示工资的名词，以及为错误付出的更大代价。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one hand pushing coins across a counter while the other hand passes goods back.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把钱推过柜台，另一只手把东西递回来。

branches.en: a card tapped on a reader
branches.cn: 在刷卡机上轻碰的卡

branches.en: a note that saves an hour of work
branches.cn: 省下一小时工夫的一行提示

branches.en: coins counted at the end of a shift
branches.cn: 下班时数过的一叠工钱

branches.en: a careless sentence that costs years
branches.cn: 一句轻率的话赔上好几年

branches.en: the same verb weighing gain and loss
branches.cn: 同一个动词在衡量所得与所失

intro.en: The root of pay is a Latin word for peace, and the family moves from quieting a person to settling a debt and then to the money that changes hands.
intro.cn: pay 的词根是拉丁语中表示和平的词，这一族词从「让人平静」走到「结清债务」，再走到易手的钱。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 付款；款项；报答
definition_en: the act of paying money, a sum of money that is paid, or something given in return for what someone has done
core_image: 一只信封从一只手递到另一只手里，封口处写着金额
scene: 月底的办公室里，会计把一叠单据摊在桌上。The company sent the payment two days before the deadline.
sceneCN: 这里是「付款、支付」（第 1 个义项：付钱这一行为）；句意为公司在截止日期前两天把款项汇出。图中可辨识物件：单据、计算器、贴着标签的信封。

derivatives.zh: 由 payment 去掉名词后缀 -ment 得到的基础动词，义为「支付」
由 pay 加 -able 构成，指应付的、可支付的
由 pay 加 -er 构成，指付款的一方
由 pay 加 -ee 构成，指收款的一方

senses.title: The act of paying money
senses.definition: the act of giving money for goods, work or a service
senses.definitionCN: 为货物、劳动或服务把钱交出去这一行为
senses.example: The company sent the payment two days before the deadline.
senses.exampleCN: 公司在截止日期前两天把款项汇出。
senses.why: The suffix -ment turns a verb into the name of its action, so payment names the handing over itself rather than the money.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ment 把动词变成动作的名称，所以 payment 先指「把钱交出去」这件事，而不是那笔钱。

senses.title: An amount of money paid
senses.definition: a sum of money that is paid or that has to be paid
senses.definitionCN: 已经付出或按约定需要付出的一笔钱
senses.example: The first payment is due at the end of the month.
senses.exampleCN: 第一期款项在月底到期。
senses.why: Once the action has a name, the thing produced by the action takes the same noun, which is why payments can be counted one by one.
senses.whyCN: 动作有了名称之后，动作产生的东西也用同一个名词，所以一笔一笔的款项可以数出来。

senses.title: A return for what someone has done
senses.definition: something given or suffered as a return for what a person has done
senses.definitionCN: 因某人做过的事而得到或承受的回报
senses.example: That was payment for years of neglect.
senses.exampleCN: 那是对多年冷落的报应。
senses.why: If paying is giving back what is owed, then any return can be called payment, and the word stretches from wages to punishment.
senses.whyCN: 既然付款是归还所欠，那么任何回报都可以叫 payment，这个词便从报酬一路延伸到惩罚。

intro.en: Payment is the English noun built on pay, and both go back through French to a Latin word for peace.
intro.cn: payment 是在 pay 之上构成的英语名词，二者都经法语回溯到一个表示和平的拉丁词。

items.en: Pax meant peace, and settling a claim was understood as restoring quiet between two sides.
items.cn: pax 意为和平，结清一笔索求被理解为让双方之间恢复安静。

items.en: The verb pacare meant to quiet or satisfy someone, and in medieval use it covered satisfying a creditor with money.
items.cn: 动词 pacare 意为使某人平静或满足，在中世纪的用法里包括用钱让债主满足。

items.en: Old French formed paiement from payer, adding its own noun ending to the verb for paying.
items.cn: 古法语由 payer 造出 paiement，给表示支付的动词加上自己的名词词尾。

items.en: Anglo-French carried the word into English legal and commercial writing, where fixed sums and dates mattered.
items.cn: 盎格鲁法语把这个词带进英语的法律与商业文书，那里讲究固定的金额与日期。

items.en: Modern English keeps payment for the act, for each sum, and for a return of any kind, while pay names the wages themselves.
items.cn: 现代英语用 payment 指行为、每一笔金额以及任何形式的回报，而 pay 指工钱本身。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the base verb, the two person forms and one word that only looks similar; the near-meaning group gathers words for sums paid and for closing an account.
note.cn: 形近组收基础动词、两个指人的形式，以及一个只是外形相似的词；近义组收表示所付金额与结清账目的词。

entries.definition: The verb that payment is built on, meaning to give money for something.
entries.definitionCN: payment 所依附的动词，意为为某物付钱。

entries.definition: That must be paid, or able to be paid.
entries.definitionCN: 应付的，或可支付的。

entries.definition: The person who receives a payment.
entries.definitionCN: 收到款项的人。

entries.definition: The hard surface beside a road, from a Latin verb meaning to beat down; only the ending looks alike.
entries.definitionCN: 路旁的硬质路面，来自一个意为「夯平」的拉丁动词；只是词尾相像，词源不同。

entries.definition: Money paid for a service or for a right.
entries.definitionCN: 为某项服务或某项权利付出的钱。

entries.definition: One of several fixed sums paid over a period.
entries.definitionCN: 分几期付出的一笔固定金额。

entries.definition: Money sent to someone, especially by post or transfer.
entries.definitionCN: 汇给某人的钱，尤指通过邮寄或转账。

entries.definition: The act of paying what is owed and ending a claim.
entries.definitionCN: 付清欠款并了结索求的行为。

normalIntro.en: The word is a verb plus a noun ending, and behind the verb sits a Latin idea of peace; the whole family is about making a claim go quiet.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是动词加名词词尾，动词背后是拉丁语中「和平」的观念；整族词都在说让一项索求安静下来。

normal.en: Payment is pay plus -ment, the ending that turns an action into a noun, as in movement and argument.
normal.cn: payment 是 pay 加 -ment，这个后缀把动作变成名词，就像 movement 与 argument。

normal.en: Old French had paiement, so English did not invent the noun; it borrowed a ready-made form.
normal.cn: 古法语已有 paiement，英语并没有自造这个名词，而是借了一个现成的形式。

normal.en: Make a payment is the everyday phrase, because the noun names the act rather than a thing you can hold.
normal.cn: make a payment 是日常说法，因为这个名词指行为，而不是手里能拿住的东西。

normal.en: A down payment is the sum handed over first, before the rest follows in instalments.
normal.cn: down payment 是先交出的那一笔，其余部分随后分期付清。

normal.en: With payment the focus is on the act or the sum; with pay it is on the wages as a whole.
normal.cn: 用 payment 时焦点在行为或某一笔钱；用 pay 时焦点在作为整体的工钱。

abstract.en: Adding -ment to a verb is a way of freezing an action into something a contract can name.
abstract.cn: 给动词加 -ment，是把一个动作冻成合同可以指名的那样东西。

abstract.en: A payment is a promise made visible: the moment an obligation turns into something countable.
abstract.cn: 一笔付款是让承诺变得可见的时刻：义务变成了可以计数的东西。

abstract.en: The word keeps the old idea that money quiets a claim, which is why even a punishment can be called its payment.
abstract.cn: 这个词保留了「钱让索求安静」的旧观念，所以连惩罚也可以被称为它的报应。

examples.en: The company sent the payment two days before the deadline.
examples.cn: 公司在截止日期前两天把款项汇出。

examples.en: The first payment is due at the end of the month.
examples.cn: 第一期款项在月底到期。

examples.en: They accept payment by card or by bank transfer.
examples.cn: 他们接受刷卡或银行转账付款。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「赔门特」——像「赔」加上一道门，钱从门里递出去；payment 就是付出去的款。

root: pay（支付）加名词后缀 -ment 构成；pay 源自拉丁语 pax（和平）与 pacare（使平静、清偿），经古法语 payer 与 paiement 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the act of handing money over; from that act come the single sum paid and the wider idea of any return, good or bad.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是把钱交出去这个动作；由它分出所付的一笔金额，以及任何回报（无论好坏）这一更宽的用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sealed envelope passing from one hand to another, an amount written across the flap.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只封好的信封从一只手递到另一只手里，封口上写着金额。

branches.en: a transfer completed before a deadline
branches.cn: 在截止前完成的一笔转账

branches.en: a numbered first sum due at month end
branches.cn: 月底到期、编号为第一期的一笔钱

branches.en: an old neglect finally answered
branches.cn: 多年的冷落终于得到回应

branches.en: the act and the sum share one noun
branches.cn: 行为与金额共用一个名词

branches.en: what is counted and what is returned
branches.cn: 被计数的那笔与被归还的那份

intro.en: The word is a Latin-rooted verb with an English noun ending, and the Latin root itself began as a word for peace.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁词根的动词加上英语名词词尾，而那个拉丁词根本身最初表示和平。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 豌豆；豌豆粒；豌豆状的小圆物
definition_en: a round green seed that grows in a long pod and is eaten as a vegetable; also a small round object that looks like this seed
core_image: 拇指沿着豆荚的缝一压，一排圆豆滚进掌心
scene: 菜园里藤蔓顺着竹架往上爬，几个鼓鼓的豆荚垂在叶子下面。He split a pod open and the small green peas rolled across the cutting board.
sceneCN: 这里是「豌豆」（第 1 个义项：长在豆荚里的绿色圆粒）；句意是他掰开一个豆荚，小小的绿豌豆滚到了砧板上。画面里有竹架、豆荚与砧板。

pos.zh: 豌豆；豌豆粒；豌豆状小圆物

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁 pisum 经古英语 pise 演变而来的旧式集体名词，后来被复数 peas 取代，义为「豌豆（总称）」
由 pea 与 sized 复合而成，义为「豌豆大小的」
由 pea 与 soup 复合而成，指用豌豆煮成的浓汤

senses.title: A round green seed grown in a pod
senses.definition: a climbing plant of the legume family, or the round green seed it bears inside a long pod
senses.definitionCN: 豆科的一种攀缘植物，或它结在长豆荚里的绿色圆粒种子
senses.example: Peas need a trellis to climb in a small garden.
senses.exampleCN: 在小菜园里，豌豆需要有个架子才能往上爬。
senses.why: Latin pisum named both the plant and its seed, so the word begins as the name of a crop rather than of a single grain.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 pisum 兼指这种植物与它的种子，所以这个词最初是作物的名字，而不是单独一粒豆的名字。

senses.title: The seed eaten as a vegetable
senses.definition: the seed harvested while still green and soft, cooked as a vegetable or sold frozen and canned
senses.definitionCN: 在仍青嫩时采收的种子，作为蔬菜烹调，或以冷冻、罐装形式出售
senses.example: She added a cup of frozen peas to the rice.
senses.exampleCN: 她往米饭里加了一杯冷冻豌豆。
senses.why: Once the crop reaches the kitchen, the same word names the food on the plate, and the plural is the usual form because peas are eaten in numbers.
senses.whyCN: 当这种作物进了厨房，同一个词就指盘中的食物；因为豌豆总是成把地吃，复数形式反而更常用。

senses.title: A small round object like a pea
senses.definition: any small round thing that resembles a pea in size or shape
senses.definitionCN: 任何在大小或形状上像豌豆的小圆物
senses.example: The beads were the size of peas and just as smooth.
senses.exampleCN: 那些珠子有豌豆大小，也一样光滑。
senses.why: A pea is a ready-made standard of smallness and roundness, so English borrows the vegetable to describe beads, pellets and other tiny spheres.
senses.whyCN: 豌豆是现成的「小而圆」的标准，于是英语借这种蔬菜来描述珠子、小丸等微小的球状物。

intro.en: Pea comes from a Latin name for the pulse, filtered through an Old English form that English later cut in two.
intro.cn: pea 来自拉丁语对这种豆类的称呼，经古英语形式传入，后来又被英语截短成现在的样子。

items.en: Pisum was the Latin name for the pea plant and its seed, and it stands behind most European names for the vegetable.
items.cn: pisum 是拉丁语中对豌豆植株及其种子的称呼，也是欧洲多数语言里这个蔬菜名称的来源。

items.en: Greek pison named the same pulse and is generally thought to come from an older Mediterranean language rather than from Greek itself.
items.cn: 希腊语 pison 指同一种豆类，一般认为它来自更早的地中海语言，而不是希腊语本身。

items.en: Old English borrowed the word as pise or pyse, a singular form that also served as a mass noun for the crop.
items.cn: 古英语借入后写作 pise 或 pyse，这个单数形式同时也当集体名词，指这种作物。

items.en: Middle English used pease for one seed and for many, so speakers began to hear the ending as a plural marker.
items.cn: 中古英语用 pease 兼指一粒和许多粒，于是人们开始把这个词尾听成复数标记。

items.en: English cut the word back to pea as a new singular and formed peas as its plural, a process known as back-formation.
items.cn: 英语把词截短成 pea 作为新的单数，再造出复数 peas，这种过程称为逆构词。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the old form of the word, a close compound and two words that merely share its sound; the near-meaning group collects other edible seeds.
note.cn: 形近组收这个词的旧形式、一个近亲复合词，以及两个只是读音相近的词；近义组收其他可食用的种子。

entries.definition: The older form of the word, now archaic or dialectal, kept alive in pease pudding.
entries.definitionCN: 这个词的旧形式，现已古旧或限于方言，保留在豌豆泥这一说法里。

entries.definition: The seed of a low plant in the same family, named by joining pea and nut.
entries.definitionCN: 同科矮生植物结的种子，由 pea 与 nut 拼合命名。

entries.definition: A hard round gem formed inside an oyster; only the spelling is close, the source is different.
entries.definitionCN: 牡蛎体内形成的坚硬圆珠；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: The pointed top of a mountain; only the sound and spelling are close, the source is different.
entries.definitionCN: 山峰的尖顶；只是读音与拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: An edible seed of a climbing plant, often kidney-shaped.
entries.definitionCN: 攀缘植物结的可食用种子，常呈肾形。

entries.definition: A small flat seed of a plant in the same family, usually cooked in soup.
entries.definitionCN: 同科植物结的小扁种子，通常煮汤食用。

entries.definition: Any plant that bears pods, or the edible seed of such a plant.
entries.definitionCN: 任何结豆荚的植物，或这类植物的可食用种子。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin seed name that English shortened twice over, so its history is a lesson in how plurals can reshape a singular.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语的种子名称，英语先后把它截短了两次，它的历史正好说明复数如何反过来重塑单数。

normal.en: Latin pisum is the oldest recorded name of the seed, and it survives almost unchanged in French pois and Italian pisello.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 pisum 是这种种子最早的名称记录，在法语 pois 与意大利语 pisello 里几乎原样保留。

normal.en: English once said pease for one seed and for many, which is why peas now sounds like a plain plural of pea.
normal.cn: 英语曾用 pease 兼指一粒与许多粒，所以今天的 peas 听起来就是 pea 的普通复数。

normal.en: A pea is defined by its pod: the seeds grow in a row inside a long case that splits along one seam.
normal.cn: 豌豆由豆荚来定义：种子成排长在一个长壳里，壳沿着一条缝裂开。

normal.en: Pea green and pea-sized both take the vegetable as a standard of colour and of smallness.
normal.cn: pea green 与 pea-sized 都拿这种蔬菜当作颜色与大小的标准。

normal.en: The noun is countable now, so one says one pea, two peas, and a bowl of peas.
normal.cn: 这个名词现在是可数的，所以说一粒豌豆、两粒豌豆、一碗豌豆。

abstract.en: A pea is a seed that carries its own food and its own case, a small complete package.
abstract.cn: 豌豆是一粒自带养料、自带外壳的种子，一个小而完整的包裹。

abstract.en: The word shrank from pease to pea because speakers rebuilt a singular out of a plural they had misheard.
abstract.cn: 这个词从 pease 缩成 pea，是因为说话人把自己听错的复数重新造成了单数。

abstract.en: Anything small, round and green can be called pea-like, which shows how a vegetable becomes a unit of size.
abstract.cn: 凡是小而圆、颜色发绿的东西都能说成像豌豆，这显示一种蔬菜如何变成大小的单位。

examples.en: She shelled a bowl of peas for dinner.
examples.cn: 她剥了一碗豌豆准备做晚饭。

examples.en: The soup was thick with split peas and ham.
examples.cn: 汤里满是干豌豆和火腿，十分浓稠。

examples.en: Each bead was the size of a pea and smooth as glass.
examples.cn: 每颗珠子都有豌豆大小，光滑得像玻璃。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「皮」——剥开豆荚那层皮，里面就是豌豆；pea 就是豌豆。

root: 来自拉丁语 pisum（豌豆），经古英语 pise、中古英语 pease 演变，近代英语逆构出单数 pea；与表示和平的 peace 只是同音，来源完全不同。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the seed inside the pod; the senses move from the growing crop to the food on the plate and then to any tiny round thing.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是豆荚里的种子；义项从地里的作物，移到盘中的食物，再移到任何微小的圆物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thumb pressing the seam of a pod until a row of round seeds rolls into the palm.
core.cn: 核心意象：拇指压开豆荚的缝，一排圆豆滚进掌心。

branches.en: a vine climbing a bamboo frame in a kitchen garden
branches.cn: 菜园里顺着竹架往上爬的藤

branches.en: a pod splitting open above a dinner plate
branches.cn: 餐盘上方裂开的豆荚

branches.en: a cup of frozen peas tipped into boiling rice
branches.cn: 一杯冻豌豆倒进沸着的米饭

branches.en: beads rolling across a table, each the size of a seed
branches.cn: 滚过桌面的珠子，颗颗如豆

branches.en: a seed used as a measure for anything very small
branches.cn: 拿豆粒来衡量极细小之物的做法

intro.en: The word comes down from a Latin name for the seed, filtered through an Old English form that English later cut in two.
intro.cn: 这个词源自拉丁语中表示种子的名称，经古英语形式过滤，后来又被英语截成两段。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。
