definition_zh: 和平；安宁；和睦；和约
definition_en: a state in which there is no war or fighting; also calm and quiet, friendly relations between people, or a treaty that ends a war
core_image: 两双原本握着武器的手松开，掌心向上放在桌上
scene: 战事停下的那个清晨，街上第一次没有枪声，人们推开窗，听见鸟叫。After years of fighting, the two sides finally agreed to make peace.
sceneCN: 这里是「和平」（第 1 个义项：没有战争的状态）；句意是打了多年之后，双方终于同意讲和。画面里有安静的街道、推开的窗与窗外的鸟。

collocations.zh: 处于和平状态；内心平静

derivatives.zh: 由 peace 加形容词词尾 -ful 构成，义为「和平的；宁静的」
由 peace 加 -able 构成，义为「爱好和平的；不爱争执的」
由 peace 与 keeping 复合而成，指以武力或派驻人员维持停火的工作
由 peace 与 time 复合而成，指没有战争的时期

senses.title: Freedom from war
senses.definition: a condition in which nations or groups are not fighting each other
senses.definitionCN: 国家或群体之间不再交战的状态
senses.example: The two countries have lived in peace for fifty years.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个国家已经和平相处了五十年。
senses.why: Latin pax named a pact that ended a quarrel, so peace begins as an agreement rather than as a feeling.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 pax 指结束争执的约定，所以 peace 的起点是一份协议，而不是一种心情。

senses.title: Calm and quiet
senses.definition: a state of quiet and calm, free from noise, worry or disturbance
senses.definitionCN: 没有噪声、忧虑或打扰的安静平和状态
senses.example: She longed for peace after a day in the noisy market.
senses.exampleCN: 在吵闹的市场待了一天之后，她渴望安宁。
senses.why: The public sense of a stopped war can be felt by one person as a stopped noise, so the word moves inward from the battlefield to the mind.
senses.whyCN: 公共意义上「战争停止」的感受，落实到个人身上就是「噪声停止」，于是这个词从战场转向了内心。

senses.title: Friendly relations between people
senses.definition: a state in which people are not quarrelling and treat each other in a friendly way
senses.definitionCN: 人们不再争吵、彼此以友好方式相处的状态
senses.example: The brothers made peace after a long silence.
senses.exampleCN: 两兄弟在长久互不理睬之后和好了。
senses.why: Scale the same absence of conflict down to a family or a pair of neighbours, and the word still means that nobody is at war.
senses.whyCN: 把同一种「没有冲突」缩小到家庭或两个邻居身上，这个词仍然表示没有人处在交战状态。

senses.title: A treaty that ends a war
senses.definition: an agreement in which two sides formally stop fighting and settle their differences
senses.definitionCN: 双方正式停止交战并解决分歧的协议
senses.example: The peace was signed in a small town hall.
senses.exampleCN: 和约在一座小镇的礼堂里签署。
senses.why: Because pax first meant the agreement itself, the word can name the signed document and not only the state that follows it.
senses.whyCN: 既然 pax 最早指协议本身，这个词就能指签署的文件，而不只是协议带来的状态。

intro.en: Peace goes back to a Latin noun for a pact, and it has never lost the idea that peace is something two sides agree to.
intro.cn: peace 可追到拉丁语中表示约定的名词，它始终没有丢掉「和平是双方谈成的事」这一层意思。

items.en: Pax meant a pact or agreement that ended a quarrel, and it also named the state that followed such an agreement.
items.cn: pax 意为结束争执的约定或协议，也指协议达成之后的状态。

items.en: The genitive pacis supplied the stem seen in pacific and pacify, words about making or keeping agreement.
items.cn: 它的属格 pacis 提供了 pacific 与 pacify 所用的词干，这些词都与缔结或维持和约有关。

items.en: Old French pais carried the Latin noun into French with the sense of peace and quiet.
items.cn: 古法语 pais 把这一拉丁名词带入法语，义为和平与安宁。

items.en: Middle English wrote the word as pees or pes, and it covered both public peace and personal calm.
items.cn: 中古英语写作 pees 或 pes，既指公共的和平，也指个人的平静。

items.en: Modern English settled on the spelling peace and kept the whole range from treaties to a quiet mind.
items.cn: 现代英语把拼写固定为 peace，并保留了从和约到内心宁静的整套含义。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the Latin family of pax and one word that only sounds the same; the near-meaning group collects states of calm and of agreement.
note.cn: 形近组收的是 pax 这一拉丁词族，另加一个只是读音相同的词；近义组收表示平静与意见一致的状态。

entries.definition: A formal agreement between two sides, usually to stop conflict or to cooperate.
entries.definitionCN: 双方达成的正式协议，通常用于停止冲突或开展合作。

entries.definition: Peaceful in intention; also the name of the great ocean.
entries.definitionCN: 意图和平的；也用作大洋的名称。

entries.definition: To calm someone who is angry, or to end fighting.
entries.definitionCN: 使发怒的人平静下来，或平息争斗。

entries.definition: The round green seed eaten as a vegetable; it only sounds like peace, the source is different.
entries.definitionCN: 作蔬菜食用的绿色圆粒；只是读音与 peace 相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A state of being free from worry, movement or noise.
entries.definitionCN: 没有忧虑、动静或噪声的状态。

entries.definition: A state in which people agree and work well together.
entries.definitionCN: 人们意见一致、相处融洽的状态。

entries.definition: An agreement to stop fighting for a period of time.
entries.definitionCN: 在一定时期内停止交战的协议。

entries.definition: Little or no noise; a still and restful condition.
entries.definitionCN: 几乎没有声响；安静而宜人的状态。

normalIntro.en: The word starts as a signed agreement and widens until it can describe a single quiet room.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从一纸签下的协议出发，一步步扩大，直到能描述一间安静的房间。

normal.en: Pax was a pact, so peace in Latin begins as an agreement rather than as a feeling.
normal.cn: pax 本是一份约定，所以拉丁语里的和平最初是协议，而不是感受。

normal.en: Pacific and pacify share the same stem, which is why all three words are about making or keeping agreement.
normal.cn: pacific 与 pacify 共用同一词干，所以这三个词都与缔结或维持和约有关。

normal.en: English once wrote pees, which is why the modern spelling looks nothing like the Latin pax.
normal.cn: 英语曾把这个词写作 pees，所以今天的拼写与拉丁语 pax 几乎看不出关系。

normal.en: At peace can describe a country and a mind, because the word covers both public and private calm.
normal.cn: at peace 既能说一个国家，也能说一颗心，因为这个词同时覆盖公共与私人的平静。

normal.en: Peace is usually uncountable, but the plural peaces appears when several separate treaties are compared.
normal.cn: peace 通常不可数，但比较几份各自独立的和约时会出现复数 peaces。

abstract.en: Peace is not the absence of anything but the presence of an agreement that both sides intend to keep.
abstract.cn: 和平不是什么东西消失了，而是双方都打算遵守的那份约定还在。

abstract.en: The same word serves a signed treaty and a quiet evening, suggesting that outer order and inner quiet are made of the same material.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既服务于签署的和约，也服务于安静的夜晚，暗示外在秩序与内心安静由同一种材料做成。

abstract.en: A word that began as a handshake now names what whole nations hope for.
abstract.cn: 一个从握手开始的词，如今成了整个国家的愿望。

examples.en: The treaty brought peace to the region after a long war.
examples.cn: 这项条约在长期战事之后为该地区带来了和平。

examples.en: She sat by the window and enjoyed the peace of the early morning.
examples.cn: 她坐在窗边，享受清晨的安宁。

examples.en: The two neighbours finally made peace after months of silence.
examples.cn: 两位邻居在数月互不理睬之后终于和好。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「皮斯」——把武器收起来，世界就安静了；peace 就是和平。

root: 来自拉丁语 pax（和约、和平），属格 pacis，经古法语 pais 进入英语；同族词有 pact、pacific、pacify。与表示豌豆的 pea 只是同音，来源完全不同。

sensesIntro.en: The core is an agreement that stops a quarrel; the senses run from war between nations, to quiet around a person, to peace between neighbours, and back to the signed treaty itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是让争执停下的约定；义项从国家之间的战争，到人身边的安静，到邻里之间的和睦，最后再回到签署的和约本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands that once held weapons opening and resting flat on a table.
core.cn: 核心意象：两双原本握着武器的手松开，掌心向上放在桌上。

branches.en: a morning when the guns finally fall silent
branches.cn: 枪声终于停下的清晨

branches.en: a quiet window opened to birdsong
branches.cn: 推开窗户听见鸟叫的安静时刻

branches.en: two brothers shaking hands after a long silence
branches.cn: 两兄弟在长久沉默后握的手

branches.en: a treaty signed on a plain wooden desk
branches.cn: 在朴素木桌上签署的和约

branches.en: one word holding a nation, a room and a friendship
branches.cn: 一个词同时托住国家、房间与友情

intro.en: A Latin noun of agreement, its oblique stem and a French reshaping hold the word together, with -ful and -able branching off it.
intro.cn: 一个表示约定的拉丁名词、它的斜格词干以及法语的重塑共同支撑这个词，-ful 与 -able 又从它分出新的词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: the work of keeping a truce

definition_zh: 和平的；宁静的；平和的
definition_en: without war or fighting; quiet and calm; or gentle in temperament and not eager to argue
core_image: 午后的院子没有风，一只猫在阳光下慢慢闭上眼睛
scene: 乡下的小院只听得见虫鸣，竹椅上的人把书合上，任由阳光落在膝头。It was a peaceful afternoon, and nobody wanted to break the silence.
sceneCN: 这里是「宁静的」（第 2 个义项：环境安静、不被打扰）；句意是那是一个宁静的下午，谁也不愿打破这份安静。画面里有小院、虫鸣、竹椅与合上的书。

derivatives.zh: 由 peaceful 加副词词尾 -ly 构成，义为「平和地；安静地」
由 peaceful 加名词词尾 -ness 构成，义为「宁静；平和」
由 peaceful 加否定前缀 un- 构成，义为「不平静的；不安宁的」

senses.title: Free from war or violence
senses.definition: describing a place, time or solution in which there is no war or fighting
senses.definitionCN: 形容没有战争或暴力的地方、时期或解决办法
senses.example: They hoped for a peaceful settlement of the dispute.
senses.exampleCN: 他们希望这场争端能得到和平解决。
senses.why: Peace plus -ful means full of peace, and the first and most public kind of peace is the absence of war.
senses.whyCN: peace 加 -ful 意为「充满和平」，而最公开、最基本的一种和平就是没有战争。

senses.title: Quiet and undisturbed
senses.definition: quiet and calm, with nothing loud, hurried or troubling going on
senses.definitionCN: 安静平和，没有喧闹、匆忙或令人烦扰的事情发生
senses.example: The village was peaceful at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 黎明时分的村子十分宁静。
senses.why: If a country can be full of peace, so can a room; the same adjective simply shifts from public order to the feel of a place.
senses.whyCN: 既然一个国家可以「充满和平」，一间屋子也可以；同一个形容词只是从公共秩序转到地方的氛围上。

senses.title: Gentle and not inclined to argue
senses.definition: having a calm temper and avoiding quarrels or violence
senses.definitionCN: 性情温和，避免争吵或使用暴力
senses.example: He is a peaceful man who avoids quarrels.
senses.exampleCN: 他是个平和的人，遇事总避开争吵。
senses.why: Push the adjective inside a person and it describes someone who carries the same absence of conflict in their temper.
senses.whyCN: 把这个形容词推进一个人心里，它描述的就是把同一种「不起冲突」带进性情的人。

intro.en: Peaceful is a plain English compound: a Latin noun for agreement, filtered through French, plus the old suffix that means full of.
intro.cn: peaceful 是一个朴素的英语复合词：经法语过滤的拉丁语「约定」名词，加上表示「充满」的古老词尾。

items.en: Pax named an agreement and the state that followed it, and its stem pac- feeds the whole family of peace words.
items.cn: pax 指约定以及约定之后的状态，其词干 pac- 支撑起整个和平词族。

items.en: Old French pais brought the noun to England with the sense of peace and quiet.
items.cn: 古法语 pais 把这个名词带进英格兰，义为和平与安宁。

items.en: Middle English pees named both public peace and personal calm, and it could already take the adjective ending.
items.cn: 中古英语 pees 兼具公共和平与个人平静两义，并且已经可以接形容词词尾。

items.en: The suffix -full meant full of or marked by, and it survives in modern English as the shorter -ful.
items.cn: 词尾 -full 意为「充满……的」，在现代英语中简化为更短的 -ful。

items.en: Modern English joined the two parts and spread the adjective from politics to places and to people.
items.cn: 现代英语把两部分合成 peaceful，并把这个形容词从政治扩展到地方与人的性情。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the noun and the other words built on the same Latin stem; the near-meaning group collects adjectives for quiet and untroubled conditions.
note.cn: 形近组收那个名词以及建立在同一拉丁词干上的其他词；近义组收形容安静无忧状态的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun meaning freedom from war or a state of calm.
entries.definitionCN: 表示没有战争或心境安宁的名词。

entries.definition: In a quiet and calm way, without fighting.
entries.definitionCN: 以安静平和的方式，没有争斗。

entries.definition: Willing to avoid argument; fond of peace.
entries.definitionCN: 愿意避免争执的；爱好和平的。

entries.definition: To calm an angry person, or to end violence.
entries.definitionCN: 使愤怒的人平静，或终止暴力。

entries.definition: Not excited, worried or disturbed.
entries.definitionCN: 不激动、不担忧、不被打扰的。

entries.definition: Quiet and peaceful, often used of places and water.
entries.definitionCN: 安静平和的，常用于地方与水面。

entries.definition: Calm and untroubled, with a feeling of deep quiet.
entries.definitionCN: 平静无忧、带有深沉宁静感的。

entries.definition: Making little or no noise.
entries.definitionCN: 几乎没有声响的。

normalIntro.en: The adjective is the noun plus a suffix, so every sense can be read as a kind of fullness of peace.
normalIntro.cn: 这个形容词就是名词加一个词尾，因此每个义项都可以读成某种「满是和平」的状态。

normal.en: Peaceful is peace plus -ful, so it literally means full of peace.
normal.cn: peaceful 就是 peace 加 -ful，字面意思就是「充满和平」。

normal.en: The suffix keeps a single l, unlike the separate word full.
normal.cn: 这个词尾只写一个 l，与单独成词的 full 不同。

normal.en: A peaceful place is one where nothing disturbs you, which is the calm sense of the noun pushed outward.
normal.cn: 宁静的地方就是没有什么来打扰你的地方，这是名词「平静」义向外推的结果。

normal.en: A peaceful person is not weak; the word describes someone who chooses not to quarrel.
normal.cn: 平和的人并不软弱；这个词描述的是选择不争吵的人。

normal.en: The comparative takes more and most because the adjective is too long for -er and -est.
normal.cn: 比较级用 more、最高级用 most，因为这个词太长，不能加 -er 与 -est。

abstract.en: Peaceful describes a condition rather than an act: it says what is missing, namely noise and conflict.
abstract.cn: peaceful 描述的是状态而不是动作：它说的是缺少了什么，即噪声与冲突。

abstract.en: The same adjective can qualify a village, an afternoon and a man, because calmness looks alike in all three.
abstract.cn: 同一个形容词能修饰村庄、下午和人，因为安静在三者身上看起来很像。

abstract.en: A word made by adding full to peace suggests that peace is a substance one can be filled with.
abstract.cn: 把 full 加到 peace 上构成的词，暗示和平是一种可以被充满的东西。

examples.en: The two states reached a peaceful agreement.
examples.cn: 这两个国家达成了和平协议。

examples.en: It was a peaceful evening with no traffic and no voices.
examples.cn: 那是一个没有车声、没有人语的宁静夜晚。

examples.en: She has a peaceful way of settling arguments.
examples.cn: 她有一种平和的化解争执的方式。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「皮斯佛」——满心都是 peace，人就平和了；peaceful 是平和的。

root: 由名词 peace（和平）加形容词词尾 -ful（充满……的）构成；peace 来自拉丁语 pax，属格 pacis，经古法语 pais 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a place or person filled with peace; the senses divide into the public absence of war, the quiet of a place, and the gentleness of a temper.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是充满和平的地方或人；义项分出公共层面的没有战争、地方的安静，以及性情的温和。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a courtyard without wind, where a cat slowly closes its eyes in the sun.
core.cn: 核心意象：没有风的午后小院，一只猫在阳光下慢慢闭上眼睛。

branches.en: two delegations signing a settlement instead of fighting
branches.cn: 两个代表团以签署协议代替开战

branches.en: a courtyard where only insects can be heard
branches.cn: 只听得见虫鸣的小院

branches.en: a man who lowers his voice when others begin to shout
branches.cn: 别人开始喊时反而放低声音的人

branches.en: a public truce and a private temper sharing one word
branches.cn: 公共的停火与私人的性情共用一个词

branches.en: a quiet afternoon and a quiet man
branches.cn: 安静的下午与安静的人

intro.en: The word is the noun peace with the old suffix -ful, so its parts are a Latin root of agreement and an English marker of fullness.
intro.cn: 这个词是名词 peace 加古老词尾 -ful，因此它的成分是一个表示约定的拉丁词根，和一个标示「充满」的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 山峰；顶点；峰值；帽檐；达到最高点
definition_en: the pointed top of a mountain; the highest point or maximum of anything; the front edge of a cap; to reach a maximum
core_image: 一条上升的线越来越陡，最后收成一个尖，然后开始下落
scene: 登山队在最后一段岩壁上放慢脚步，前方只剩一小块尖顶。Only a narrow peak remained above the last stretch of rock.
sceneCN: 此处指「山体最上端的尖顶」（第 1 个义项：山脊收束成的最高尖点）；句意为最后一段岩壁之上只剩一个狭窄的尖顶。图中可辨识物件：岩壁、狭窄的尖顶、登山绳、放慢脚步的队员；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 山峰；山顶；最高点；峰值；帽檐；尖端
高峰的；峰值的（作定语，如 peak hours）

derivatives.zh: 有尖顶的；（脸色）憔悴的
憔悴的；尖耸的
无尖顶的；无帽檐的
非高峰的；错峰地
峰值负荷

senses.title: The pointed top of a mountain
senses.definition: the sharp upper end of a mountain, where its slopes meet
senses.definitionCN: 山体最上端的尖点，坡面在此交会
senses.example: Only a narrow peak remained above the last stretch of rock.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一段岩壁之上只剩一个狭窄的尖顶。
senses.why: The earliest sense is a pointed top: the word names the shape where two slopes finally meet.
senses.whyCN: 最早的义项是「尖顶」：这个词命名两条坡面最终相交的那个形状。

senses.title: The highest point of a climb
senses.definition: the top that a climber reaches after ascending a mountain
senses.definitionCN: 攀登者上到山顶后所抵达的最高处
senses.example: They reached the peak just before the clouds closed in.
senses.exampleCN: 他们赶在云雾合拢之前登上了顶峰。
senses.why: A climb ends at the highest point, so the top became the goal of the whole action.
senses.whyCN: 攀登在最高点结束，于是这个顶端成了整个动作的目标。

senses.title: The high point of a career or period
senses.definition: the moment of greatest success or intensity in a process
senses.definitionCN: 一个过程中最成功或最强烈的时刻
senses.example: Her career reached its peak in the early nineties.
senses.exampleCN: 她的事业在九十年代初达到顶峰。
senses.why: A curve that rises and falls gives the metaphor: the best moment is the point where the line stops climbing.
senses.whyCN: 先升后落的曲线提供了比喻：最好的时刻就是那条线停止上升的那一点。

senses.title: A maximum value in data
senses.definition: the highest value recorded in a series, graph or measurement
senses.definitionCN: 在一组数据、图表或测量中记录到的最高值
senses.example: The graph shows a sharp peak around noon.
senses.exampleCN: 图表显示中午前后有一个陡峭的峰值。
senses.why: Statistics keeps the geometry literal: the maximum is drawn as the top of a curve.
senses.whyCN: 统计学保留了字面的几何形状：最大值被画成曲线的顶端。

senses.title: The busiest period
senses.definition: the time when traffic, demand or activity is greatest
senses.definitionCN: 交通、需求或活动最旺盛的时段
senses.example: Trains are crowded during peak hours.
senses.exampleCN: 高峰时段火车很拥挤。
senses.why: If activity is a curve, the busiest hour is where the curve peaks; the noun then names that hour.
senses.whyCN: 如果活动是一条曲线，最忙的那一小时就是曲线到达顶点之处；名词随后就指那个小时。

senses.title: The front edge of a cap
senses.definition: the projecting front part of a cap that shades the eyes
senses.definitionCN: 帽子前方突出、用来遮住眼睛的部分
senses.example: He pulled his cap down by the peak.
senses.exampleCN: 他抓住帽檐把帽子往下拉。
senses.why: A cap's brim projects forward and comes to a point, so the same shape word applies to clothing.
senses.whyCN: 帽檐向前突出并收成一个尖，同一个形状词于是也用于衣物。

senses.title: A projecting tip of anything
senses.titleCN: 任何物体的尖端或突出部
senses.definition: the pointed projecting part of a roof, beard or other object
senses.definitionCN: 屋顶、胡须或其他物体尖而突出的部分
senses.example: Rain ran off the peak of the tent.
senses.exampleCN: 雨水从帐篷的尖顶流下。
senses.why: The shape, not the mountain, is the core: any surface that rises to a point has a peak.
senses.whyCN: 核心是形状而不是山：任何升到一点的表面都有这样一个尖顶。

senses.title: To reach a maximum
senses.definition: to rise to the highest level and then stop rising
senses.definitionCN: 上升到最高水平后不再上升
senses.example: Sales peaked in December and fell sharply afterwards.
senses.exampleCN: 销量在十二月见顶，随后急剧下降。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb: something peaks when it reaches the top of its own curve.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动词：某物到达自身曲线的顶端，就是「见顶」。

intro.en: Peak is a northern English word of uncertain Germanic origin; the mountain sense and the figurative senses developed in later centuries. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: peak 是一个来源不确定的英格兰北部词，属日耳曼语系；山的义项与比喻义是后来几个世纪发展出来的，年代均为约数。

items.en: Middle English pek, recorded in the fourteenth century, meant 'a pointed top or projecting point', not specifically a mountain.
items.cn: 中古英语 pek 见于 14 世纪，意为「尖顶或突出的尖端」，并不专指山。

items.en: The form is probably related to Old English pēac 'pinnacle' and to a reconstructed *pēc 'pointed hill'; both are uncertain and the exact link is disputed.
items.cn: 这一形式可能与古英语 pēac「尖塔、尖顶」以及重构形式 *pēc「尖山」有关；两者都不确定，具体关联仍有争议。

items.en: Similar words appear in Middle Low German and Dutch, which supports a Germanic origin, though no single source form can be pointed to with confidence.
items.cn: 中古低地德语与荷兰语中有相似词，这支持日耳曼语来源，但无法有把握地指出某一个唯一的来源形式。

items.en: The specific sense 'pointed top of a mountain' is recorded in the sixteenth century, and 'the highest point of a mountain' became standard in the eighteenth.
items.cn: 「山峰的尖顶」这一具体义项见于 16 世纪，而「山的最高点」在 18 世纪成为通行用法。

items.en: From the late eighteenth century peak was used for the highest point of anything, including careers and graphs; the transport sense 'peak hours' belongs to the twentieth century.
items.cn: 从 18 世纪晚期起，peak 用于任何事物的最高点，包括事业与图表；交通义「高峰时段」则属于 20 世纪。

items.en: Source uncertain (root and first date): the pre-Germanic origin is unknown, the Old English connection is a hypothesis, and the earliest citations are approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根与首见年代）：日耳曼语之前的来源不明，与古英语的关联只是假说，最早书证年代为约数。

note.en: The first group is made of exact or near homophones that are constantly confused in writing; the second holds words for the top of something.
note.cn: 第一组是书写中极易混淆的同音或近音词；第二组是表示「某物顶端」的词。

entries.definition: To look quickly or secretly; the spelling with double e marks the glance, not the summit.
entries.definitionCN: 快速地或偷偷地看一眼；双 e 的拼写标记「瞥一眼」，与山顶无关。

entries.definition: To annoy someone, or to stimulate interest; it comes from French piquer 'to prick', a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 激怒某人，或激起兴趣；来自法语 piquer「刺」，词根不同。

entries.definition: The past tense of the verb or an adjective meaning 'having a peak'; as an adjective it can also mean pale and ill-looking.
entries.definitionCN: 动词过去式，或表示「有尖顶的」形容词；作形容词时还可指面色苍白、有病容。

entries.definition: A bird's bill; the vowel is the same but the first consonant is /b/, not /p/.
entries.definitionCN: 鸟喙；元音相同，但首辅音是 /b/ 而非 /p/。

entries.definition: The highest point of a mountain, used especially of reaching it and of top-level meetings; it is more formal than peak.
entries.definitionCN: 山的最高点，尤用于「登顶」与首脑会议；比 peak 更正式。

entries.definition: The highest point of a shape or system, used in geometry and formal writing; it is a Latin loan and does not name a mountain by itself.
entries.definitionCN: 形状或系统的最高点，用于几何与正式写作；它是拉丁借词，本身不指山。

entries.definition: The top line of a ridge or wave rather than a single point; a crest can be long, a peak is sharp.
entries.definitionCN: 山脊或波浪的顶线，而不是一个点；crest 可以是长的，peak 是尖的。

entries.definition: The highest part of anything, in everyday speech; it lacks the sharp, pointed image that peak carries.
entries.definitionCN: 日常语中任何事物的最高部分；它没有 peak 那种尖锐的意象。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real spelling contrasts with peek and pique, and the real phrases that mark the senses.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：与 peek、pique 的真实拼写对比，以及标记各义项的真实搭配。

normal.en: peak (mountain) vs peek (glance) vs pique (prick of annoyance): three spellings, one sound.
normal.cn: peak（山）对 peek（瞥）对 pique（被刺恼）：三个拼写，一个读音。

normal.en: The shape is a curve: rise, top, fall — the top is the peak.
normal.cn: 形状是一条曲线：上升、到顶、下落——顶端就是 peak。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: reach the peak, peak hours, peak season, at its peak.
normal.cn: 固定搭配有 reach the peak、peak hours、peak season、at its peak。

normal.en: A cap has a peak, and so does a tent; anything pointed upward qualifies.
normal.cn: 帽子有帽檐，帐篷也有尖顶；凡是向上收成尖的东西都算。

normal.en: As a verb it only means 'reach the maximum', never 'climb a mountain'.
normal.cn: 作动词时只表示「达到最大值」，从不表示「爬山」。

abstract.en: Picture a fever chart that climbs all night and turns over at dawn.
abstract.cn: 想象一张体温曲线整夜攀升，在黎明时翻转而下。

abstract.en: Picture a wave that holds its highest drop for one second before breaking.
abstract.cn: 想象一道浪在崩碎前把最高的水滴保持一秒钟。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd that fills a station at eight and is gone by nine.
abstract.cn: 想象人群在八点塞满车站，到九点又散尽。

examples.en: The peak was hidden by cloud for most of the afternoon.
examples.cn: 整个下午大部分时间，山峰都被云遮着。

examples.en: Demand for electricity peaks on the coldest evenings.
examples.cn: 最冷的傍晚用电需求达到峰值。

examples.en: Avoid the peak hours if you are driving to the airport.
examples.cn: 如果开车去机场，避开高峰时段。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「劈（pi）+ 克（k）」—— 一刀劈下去，山顶被削成一个尖 → 山峰；顶点

root: 中古英语 pek「尖顶」，可能上溯至古英语 pēac「尖塔」或重构的 *pēc「尖山」，属日耳曼语系；更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all rest on one shape: a line rises to a single sharp top, whether that line is rock, a career, a graph, a timetable, a cap or a tent.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都立在一个形状上：一条线升到一个尖顶，无论这条线是岩石、事业、图表、时刻表、帽子还是帐篷。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rising line that steepens into a point and then turns down.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条上升的线越来越陡，收成一点，然后向下转折。

branches.en: SHAPE: any surface that ends in a point has a peak, from rock to canvas.
branches.cn: 形状：凡是收成一点的表面都有尖端，从岩石到帆布都算。

branches.en: GOAL: the top is what the climb aims at.
branches.cn: 目标：顶端就是攀登所指向的东西。

branches.en: CURVE: the best moment and the highest number are both the top of a line.
branches.cn: 曲线：最好的时刻与最高的数值都是某条线的顶端。

branches.en: TIME: the busiest hour is the hour when activity is at its top.
branches.cn: 时间：最忙的那一小时，就是活动到达顶端的那一小时。

branches.en: EDGE AND ACTION: a cap's brim is a forward point, and to peak is to reach the top.
branches.cn: 边缘与动作：帽檐是向前的尖，而 peak 作动词就是到达顶端。

intro.en: Peak is a bare Germanic stem with only a few English extensions; most of its family is compounds rather than suffixes.
intro.cn: peak 是一个光秃的日耳曼语词干，英语派生有限；它的词族多为复合词而非后缀派生。

latinIntro.en: No Latin etymon is recoverable: peak goes back to an uncertain Germanic form, so the Latin entry list is empty by design.
latinIntro.cn: 无法追溯到拉丁词源：peak 上溯至一个不确定的日耳曼语形式，因此拉丁条目按规则留空。

items.exampleCN: 从公路上就能看见那个尖顶。

items.meaningCN: 多个尖顶；（他、她、它）达到峰值
items.example: Two peaks rise behind the lake.

in the act of reaching a maximum

items.example: The road is jammed in peak hours.

items.example: The grid struggles at peak load.
items.exampleCN: 电网在峰值负荷时吃紧。

definition_zh: 奇怪的；特有的；专属的；有点不舒服的
definition_en: strange or unusual in a way that is hard to explain; belonging only to one person or thing; or, in British informal use, feeling slightly unwell
core_image: 一把只配一把锁的旧钥匙，齿形古怪得让人多看两眼
scene: 旧货摊的角落里躺着一只木盒，锁孔的形状歪歪扭扭，摊主说整条街只有一把钥匙能开它。There was a peculiar smell in the attic, like old paper and rain.
sceneCN: 这里是「奇怪的」（第 1 个义项：说不清理由地反常）；句意是阁楼里有一股怪味，像旧纸混着雨水。画面里有旧货摊、歪斜的锁孔与积尘的阁楼。

pos.zh: 奇怪的；特有的；专属的；有点不舒服的

derivatives.zh: 由 peculiar 加 -ity 构成，义为「古怪之处；特性」
由 peculiar 加 -ly 构成，义为「奇怪地；尤其」
由 peculiar 与 looking 复合而成，义为「模样古怪的」

senses.title: Strange in a way that is hard to explain
senses.definition: unusual or odd in a way that makes people look twice and wonder why
senses.definitionCN: 反常或古怪到让人多看一眼、想不出原因的程度
senses.example: A peculiar noise came from the empty room.
senses.exampleCN: 空房间里传来一阵怪声。
senses.why: Latin peculiaris first meant belonging to one person alone, and what belongs to one place or one owner soon looks unlike everything around it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 peculiaris 最初意为只属于某一个人，而只属于某一地或某一主人的东西，很快就在周围显得与众不同。

senses.title: Belonging only to one person or thing
senses.definition: existing only in one particular place, group or thing and nowhere else
senses.definitionCN: 只存在于某一地点、群体或事物之中，别处没有
senses.example: This custom is peculiar to the island.
senses.exampleCN: 这种习俗是这个岛所特有的。
senses.why: The oldest layer of the word is ownership, and ownership is exactly what the phrase peculiar to still states: this belongs here and to nobody else.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的一层是「归谁所有」，而 peculiar to 这个说法说的正是这一点：它属于这里，不属于别处。

senses.title: Feeling slightly unwell
senses.definition: feeling slightly ill or strange in the body, used in informal British speech
senses.definitionCN: 在英式口语中表示身体略有不适或感觉异样
senses.example: I felt peculiar after the second cup of coffee.
senses.exampleCN: 喝完第二杯咖啡后我觉得有点不舒服。
senses.why: When the body is not its usual self, the feeling is also hard to name, so informal English reaches for the word that already means not quite right.
senses.whyCN: 当身体不在平常状态时，这种感觉也难以命名，于是口语就借用了本来就表示「不太对劲」的那个词。

intro.en: Peculiar begins with cattle: a Latin word for livestock became a word for private property, then for what belongs to one owner, and finally for what looks odd to everyone else.
intro.cn: peculiar 从牲畜讲起：拉丁语中表示家畜的词先变成「私产」，再指只属于某一主人的东西，最后指在别人眼里古怪的东西。

items.en: Pecus meant cattle, and in an economy counted in herds, livestock were the clearest visible form of wealth.
items.cn: pecus 意为牛群牲畜；在以牲畜计财的经济里，牲畜就是最清楚可见的财富形式。

items.en: Peculium was the private savings that a person, often a slave, could hold as personal property.
items.cn: peculium 指个人（常是奴隶）可以持有的私产积蓄。

items.en: Peculiaris meant belonging to one person rather than to the community, so it began as a word about ownership.
items.cn: peculiaris 意为属于某个人而非集体，所以它最初是一个谈归属的词。

items.en: Old French peculier passed the adjective into English with the sense of a possession or right that belonged to one party alone.
items.cn: 古法语 peculier 把这个形容词传入英语，指只属于一方的财物或权利。

items.en: Modern English widened the adjective from private ownership to anything marked as special, and then to what strikes us as odd.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个形容词从私人所有扩展到任何带有特殊标记的事物，再扩展到让人觉得古怪的东西。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the same Latin stem of private property; the near-meaning group collects adjectives for what is unusual or typical of one thing.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在同一「私产」拉丁词干上的词；近义组收表示反常或为某物所典型的形容词。

entries.definition: A strange detail, or the quality of belonging to one thing only.
entries.definitionCN: 奇怪的细节；或只属于某一事物的特性。

entries.definition: In a strange way, or in a way special to one person.
entries.definitionCN: 以奇怪的方式；或以某人特有的方式。

entries.definition: Connected with money, from the same Latin word for wealth.
entries.definitionCN: 与金钱有关的，来自同一个表示财富的拉丁词。

entries.definition: Unusual or surprising in a way that is hard to explain.
entries.definitionCN: 不寻常或令人惊讶、难以解释的。

entries.definition: Different from what is expected; slightly strange.
entries.definitionCN: 与预期不同、有些古怪的。

entries.definition: Strange in an interesting way, or eager to know something.
entries.definitionCN: 奇得有趣的；或好奇的。

entries.definition: Typical of a particular person or thing.
entries.definitionCN: 某一人物或事物所典型的。

normalIntro.en: A word about property turned into a word about oddity, and both meanings are still visible in its family.
normalIntro.cn: 一个谈财产的词后来变成谈古怪的词，而两层意思至今都能在它的词族里看见。

normal.en: Peculiar begins with cattle: Latin pecus gave wealth, and wealth gave the idea of property.
normal.cn: peculiar 从牲畜讲起：拉丁语 pecus 带来财富，财富又带来「财产」的观念。

normal.en: Peculium was private savings, so peculiaris meant belonging to one owner rather than to everyone.
normal.cn: peculium 是私产积蓄，所以 peculiaris 意为属于某个主人，而不是属于所有人。

normal.en: Peculiar to still keeps the old ownership sense, as in a bird peculiar to one island.
normal.cn: peculiar to 仍保留旧的归属义，例如只属于某一岛的鸟。

normal.en: The modern sense of odd grew from marking something as special, since what is special stands out from the ordinary.
normal.cn: 现代的「古怪」义从「标记为特殊」发展而来，因为特殊的东西总会从平常中显出来。

normal.en: Peculiarity and peculiarly keep the stem unchanged before the endings, with no letter dropped.
normal.cn: peculiarity 与 peculiarly 在接词尾时词干不变，也没有字母脱落。

abstract.en: Peculiar says two things at once: this belongs only here, and this does not fit everywhere else.
abstract.cn: peculiar 同时说两件事：它只属于这里，而它在别处并不合身。

abstract.en: A word born from private property now describes a private oddity, which is a small history of ownership.
abstract.cn: 一个从私产诞生的词如今描述私人的古怪，这本身就是一部小小的所有权史。

abstract.en: What is peculiar is not wrong, only marked; the word leaves room for both charm and unease.
abstract.cn: 古怪并不等于错误，只是被做了标记；这个词同时留着迷人不安两种余地。

examples.en: There was a peculiar smell in the attic.
examples.cn: 阁楼里有一股怪味。

examples.en: This bird is peculiar to the island and lives nowhere else.
examples.cn: 这种鸟为该岛所特有，别处没有。

examples.en: He looked at me in a peculiar way and said nothing.
examples.cn: 他用古怪的眼神看着我，一言不发。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「皮酷」——奇怪的皮具酷得让人多看两眼；peculiar 就是奇怪的。

root: 来自拉丁语 peculium（私产、积蓄），其源头是 pecus（牲畜）；peculiaris 意为「属于某个人的」，后经古法语 peculier 进入英语，词义从「专属」扩展到「特有」与「古怪」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is what belongs to one owner only; the senses run from private ownership to what is special to a place, and then to what looks odd because it belongs nowhere else.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是只属于某一主人的东西；义项从私人所有，到某地特有，再到因为不合于别处而显得古怪。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old key whose teeth are cut for one lock only, so everyone else finds it odd.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把只为一把锁磨出的旧钥匙，在别人眼里显得古怪。

branches.en: an attic where an unknown smell hangs in the air
branches.cn: 阁楼里说不清来源的气味

branches.en: a bird found on one island and nowhere else
branches.cn: 只在一座岛上才能见到的鸟

branches.en: a man who feels unwell after a second cup of coffee
branches.cn: 喝了第二杯咖啡后觉得不适的人

branches.en: a thing that belongs to one place and a body that does not feel itself
branches.cn: 一件只属于某地的东西，与一具不在常态的身体

branches.en: what is special to one place and what is odd to everyone
branches.cn: 对某地特有之物，与让所有人觉得古怪之物

intro.en: A Latin word for cattle lies under this adjective, and the chain of property words built on it still explains why special and strange share one form.
intro.cn: 这个形容词底下是一个表示牲畜的拉丁词，建立在它之上的财产词链至今解释了为何「特有」与「古怪」共用一个形式。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 同辈；同龄人；贵族；对等节点；凝视
definition_en: a person of the same age, rank or ability as another; a member of the British nobility; a computer linked to others as an equal; also to look closely at something
core_image: 两个人并肩站在同一级台阶上，谁也不必抬头看谁
scene: 雾很重，站牌上的字迹被水汽糊住，等车的人凑近去看。Through the fog, he peered at the sign but could not read a word.
sceneCN: 这里是「凝视、仔细看」（第 4 个义项：因看不清而凑近端详）；句意是他在雾里眯眼去看站牌，却一个字也认不出。画面里有浓雾、湿漉漉的站牌与一个前倾的身影。

pos.zh: 同辈；同龄人；贵族；对等节点

derivatives.zh: 由 peer 加表示集体或身份的 -age 构成，义为「贵族阶层；爵位」
由 peer 加表示「没有」的 -less 构成，义为「无与伦比的」
由 peer 与 pressure 复合而成，指同龄群体带来的压力

senses.title: A person of the same age or standing
senses.definition: a person who is the same age as you, or who has the same rank, ability or background
senses.definitionCN: 与你年龄相同，或地位、能力、背景相当的人
senses.example: Teenagers care a lot about the opinion of their peers.
senses.exampleCN: 青少年很在意同龄人的看法。
senses.why: Latin par meant equal, so a peer is first of all someone whose eyes are level with yours, neither above nor below.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 par 意为相等，所以 peer 首先是眼睛与你齐平的人，既不在你之上，也不在你之下。

senses.title: A member of the nobility
senses.definition: a lord who holds a title and, historically, a seat in the upper house of the British parliament
senses.definitionCN: 拥有爵位、历史上在英国上议院拥有席位的贵族
senses.example: The duke took his seat among the peers.
senses.exampleCN: 公爵在众贵族之间就座。
senses.why: Nobles of the same rank called one another equals, and the word for an equal became the name of the rank itself.
senses.whyCN: 同一等级的贵族彼此互称「同等者」，于是表示「同等者」的词就成了这个等级本身的名称。

senses.title: An equal node in a network
senses.definition: a computer or device that exchanges data with others on the same level, without a central server in charge
senses.definitionCN: 在同一层级上与其他设备交换数据、不设中央服务器的计算机或设备
senses.example: Each computer in the network acts as a peer.
senses.exampleCN: 网络中的每台计算机都作为一个对等节点工作。
senses.why: A network without a boss is a network of equals, so the old sense of an equal person was borrowed for machines that talk on equal terms.
senses.whyCN: 没有主控者的网络就是由平等者组成的网络，于是「地位相等的人」这个旧义被借去指平等通信的机器。

senses.title: To look closely at something
senses.definition: to look hard at something, especially when it is difficult to see
senses.definitionCN: 用力地看某物，尤其在不容易看清的时候
senses.example: She peered at the small print without her glasses.
senses.exampleCN: 她没戴眼镜，凑近去看那行小字。
senses.why: This verb is a separate word of uncertain origin; it may be unrelated to the noun, and dictionaries still mark its source as unclear.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词是另一个来源不确定的词，可能与名词毫无关系，词典至今仍把它的来源标为不清楚。

intro.en: The noun peer is Latin equality seen through French; the verb peer is a different word whose origin is uncertain, and the two should not be joined.
intro.cn: 名词 peer 是经法语过滤的拉丁语「相等」；动词 peer 则是另一个来源不确定的词，两者不宜混为一谈。

items.en: Par meant equal, and it still survives in English phrases about equality such as on a par with.
items.cn: par 意为相等，至今仍留在 on a par with 这类谈平等的英语说法里。

items.en: Old French per or peer carried the sense of an equal, a person of the same standing.
items.cn: 古法语 per 或 peer 带有「同等者」的意思，指地位相同的人。

items.en: Middle English peer named an equal and, by the late Middle Ages, a noble whose rank set him beside the monarch.
items.cn: 中古英语 peer 指地位相等的人，到中古后期也指其等级可与君主并列的贵族。

items.en: The nobility sense settled in this period, and peerage named the whole body of such nobles.
items.cn: 贵族这一义项在这一时期固定下来，peerage 则指这批贵族的整体。

items.en: Modern English adds the computing sense of an equal machine and keeps the verb peer, whose own source remains uncertain.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了「地位对等的机器」这一计算机义，并保留动词 peer；该动词自身的来源仍不确定。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the Latin word for equal; the near-meaning group collects words for an equal person and for steady looking.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「相等」之上的词；近义组收表示地位相同者与稳定注视的词。

entries.definition: The whole body of nobles, or the rank of a peer.
entries.definitionCN: 贵族阶层；或贵族的爵位。

entries.definition: Having no equal; better than all others.
entries.definitionCN: 无与伦比的；无人能及的。

entries.definition: The usual or expected level, from the Latin word for equal.
entries.definitionCN: 通常或预期的水平，来自拉丁语中表示相等的词。

entries.definition: The same in size, value or status.
entries.definitionCN: 在大小、价值或地位上相同的。

entries.definition: A person you work with, often of similar rank.
entries.definitionCN: 与你共事、地位常相近的人。

entries.definition: To look steadily at something for a while.
entries.definitionCN: 稳定地注视某物一段时间。

entries.definition: To look at something for a long time with open eyes.
entries.definitionCN: 睁大眼睛长时间地看。

normalIntro.en: One spelling carries two histories: a noun of equality from Latin, and a verb of looking whose source nobody can name with certainty.
normalIntro.cn: 同一个拼写背着两段历史：来自拉丁语的「平等」名词，以及来源无人能确定的「观看」动词。

normal.en: Peer and par both come from Latin par, so a peer is literally an equal.
normal.cn: peer 与 par 都来自拉丁语 par，所以 peer 字面上就是「相等者」。

normal.en: Peer review works because the judges are equals of the author, not superiors.
normal.cn: 同行评审之所以成立，是因为评审人与作者地位相等，而不是上级。

normal.en: A British peer is noble because such lords once sat as equals beside the monarch.
normal.cn: 英国的 peer 之所以指贵族，是因为这类领主曾以同等者身份与君主同坐。

normal.en: Peer-to-peer networks copy the same idea onto machines that talk without a central server.
normal.cn: 点对点网络把同一想法搬到机器上：无需中央服务器也能彼此通信。

normal.en: The verb peer is a different story: no one knows its origin for certain, so do not link it to the noun.
normal.cn: 动词 peer 是另一回事：没人确知它的来源，所以不要把它和名词挂钩。

abstract.en: A peer is someone whose eyes are level with yours, which is why the word can mean both a companion and a judge.
abstract.cn: peer 是眼睛与你齐平的人，所以这个词既能指同伴，也能指评审者。

abstract.en: Equality is the thread: it holds the schoolmate, the lord and the networked computer together.
abstract.cn: 平等是那条线：它把同学、贵族与联网的计算机串在一起。

abstract.en: The verb peer describes what you do when the world refuses to be clear, and it stands apart from all that equality.
abstract.cn: 动词 peer 描述的是世界不肯清楚时你的动作，它与那一整套平等无关。

examples.en: Children learn a great deal from their peers.
examples.cn: 孩子从同龄人那里学到很多东西。

examples.en: The paper was sent out for peer review before publication.
examples.cn: 这篇论文在发表前被送去同行评审。

examples.en: He peered into the dark room and saw nothing.
examples.cn: 他朝黑屋子里仔细看，什么也没看见。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「皮尔」——同辈人彼此平视，谁也不比谁高；peer 就是同辈。

root: 名词来自拉丁语 par（相等），经古法语 per 或 peer 进入英语，由「同等者」引申出「贵族」与「对等节点」；动词 peer（凝视）来源不确定，一般认为与名词不同源。

sensesIntro.en: The core is equality of level; the noun runs from a classmate to a lord to a machine, while the verb takes a separate path and means to look hard.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「高度齐平」；名词从同学走到贵族再走到机器，动词则另走一路，意为用力去看。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two people standing on the same step, neither having to look up.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个人并肩站在同一级台阶上，谁也不必抬头看谁。

branches.en: a circle of classmates arguing as equals
branches.cn: 围坐争论的同班同学

branches.en: a lord taking his seat in a long chamber
branches.cn: 在长长议事厅里就座的贵族

branches.en: two computers passing a file without a server
branches.cn: 两台不经过服务器直接传文件的电脑

branches.en: a face leaning toward a fogged sign
branches.cn: 凑近被雾打湿的站牌的一张脸

branches.en: equality held by a child, a lord and a machine
branches.cn: 孩子、贵族与机器共享的「平等」

intro.en: The noun rests on a Latin adjective of equality and the endings English added to it; the verb is a separate word and is flagged here rather than folded into the same root.
intro.cn: 名词建立在表示相等的拉丁形容词以及英语给它加的词尾上；动词是另一个词，这里只作标注，不并进同一词根。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。
